key: A university module: lectures
name: ch00_university_module_desk
alt: A student's study desk laid out as a university module: a laptop lecture, a thick textbook, a problem set with readings, a stack of research papers and a syllabus linking them.
scene: A slightly high, three-quarter view over a wooden study desk in a hostel room at night, lit by a warm desk lamp, with a ceiling fan blurred above and a window showing city lights. A young woman student (about 21, loose kurta, hair tied up, pencil behind her ear) sits on the right, calm and organised, one hand resting on an open syllabus sheet. Spread across the desk from left to right are five clearly separate items. Far left, an open laptop showing a paused lecture video with a teacher at a whiteboard. Next, a thick hardbound textbook, open, with coloured sticky tabs. In the middle, a stapled problem set with a few questions ticked and a small pile of photocopied extra readings clipped to it. To the right, a tall stack of research papers with dense columns and graphs, bound with a bulldog clip. Closest to her, the single-page syllabus, a neat table with rows and arrows. Thin dotted lines run from each row of the syllabus out to the laptop, the textbook and the problem set, showing which page goes with which lecture. A steel tumbler of tea sits at the corner. Mood: orderly, quiet, a plan coming together. Labels: "LECTURE" above the laptop, "TEXTBOOK" above the book, "SYLLABUS" on the sheet under her hand.

key: A bar is a zip file. Open, high
name: ch00_bar_zip_compression
alt: A long winding footpath through a day is squeezed into a small zipped pouch that keeps only four tags, with bigger pouches holding several smaller ones.
scene: A wide landscape illustration read left to right. On the left, a long winding mountain footpath drawn as a twisting line climbing and dipping across a hillside, with a tiny hiker (young man, red cap, backpack) walking it from sunrise at its start to sunset at its end; little flags mark the very first step, the highest ridge, the lowest gully and the final step. In the middle, a pair of giant hands squeezes the whole twisting path into a small cloth pouch with a zip, the path visibly sucked in like a noodle. The closed pouch on the right has only four paper tags hanging from it, one for each flag: start, highest, lowest and end; the wiggles in between are gone, shown by a faint dotted outline of the path fading out inside the pouch. Further right, five such small pouches are being zipped together into one bigger bag, and four bigger bags into a large duffel, a nesting of compressions. A small magnifying glass hovers over the large duffel showing that no wiggles survive inside. Soft morning-to-evening gradient sky behind the path. Calm, explanatory mood. Labels: "DAY" on the small pouch, "WEEK" on the bigger bag, "MONTH" on the duffel.

key: Weather vs climate. One decade is
name: ch00_weather_vs_climate
alt: A man judging the world from one dramatic stormy window beside a weather office archivist with a century of rainfall ledgers.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a middle-aged man in a striped shirt stands at a single window of a small flat, watching a dramatic monsoon storm, rain lashing, palm trees bent, lightning in the sky; his face is shocked and certain, and a thought bubble above him reads "always like this". Only one decade's calendar, ten pages, is pinned beside the window. RIGHT panel: inside an old Indian meteorological office with tall wooden shelves, an elderly archivist (grey hair, spectacles on a cord, white half-sleeve shirt) calmly pulls one ledger from a wall of a hundred identical bound rainfall registers, each spine with a year written in tiny numbers. On the desk in front of him a long paper strip chart unrolls off the table edge, showing a hundred years of ups and downs where the storm the man is watching is just one small spike among many. A brass rain gauge sits on the windowsill. Lighting: left side dark and dramatic with flashes of lightning; right side warm, dusty afternoon light through high windows. Mood: one vivid moment against patient records. Labels: "WEATHER" at the top of the left panel, "CLIMATE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A busy chat channel vs a documentation
name: ch00_chat_channel_vs_docs
alt: A brilliant answer sinks out of sight in a fast-scrolling chat while a colleague files the same answer into a tidy labelled reference binder where others find it.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a huge phone screen fills the frame, showing a group chat scrolling fast, a waterfall of message bubbles, emojis, memes and forwarded videos pouring downward. Deep at the bottom, half sunk like a coin in a well, sits one glowing golden message bubble, the great answer, with a small date tag "3 yrs ago". Above the phone, a young developer (mid 20s, hoodie, headphones round his neck) scrolls frantically with a tired, lost face. RIGHT panel: a calm office corner with a tall shelf of neatly labelled binders. A woman colleague (early 30s, glasses, cardigan, lanyard) has just clipped a copy of that same golden bubble into a binder under a clear printed tab heading; she points to it. Next to her, the same young developer now reads it easily, relieved, finger on the page, a small lightbulb above his head. A dotted arrow travels from the sunken golden bubble on the left, across the dividing line, into the binder on the right. Lighting: left panel cool and flickery blue from the screen, right panel warm and steady daylight. Mood: chaos versus order. Labels: "CHAT" at the top of the left panel, "DOCS" at the top of the right panel.

key: A lab notebook, not a sales brochure
name: ch00_notebook_vs_brochure
alt: A glossy sales brochure promising success sits next to a researcher's open lab notebook full of method notes, measurements and listed doubts.
scene: A top-down view of a laboratory bench, split by an invisible line into two halves. On the LEFT, a glossy folded sales brochure fans open: a smiling model with a thumbs-up, starbursts, a gold medal sticker, a giant tick mark and a short bold slogan "IT WORKS", all bright and shiny, with nothing underneath to back it up. A salesman's hand in a shiny suit sleeve pushes it toward the viewer. On the RIGHT, a well-worn hardback lab notebook lies open, its pages covered in handwritten columns, a small sketch of the apparatus, a table of measured values, a scribbled small graph and, at the bottom of the page, a boxed list of three points with question marks beside them, the possible flaws in the measurement. A researcher's hands (young woman, lab coat cuff, ink on one finger) hold a pencil over the notebook, about to add another doubt. Around it on the bench: a ruler, a stopwatch, a beaker and an eraser. Lighting: the brochure side has harsh, flashy highlights; the notebook side has soft even bench-lamp light. Mood: honest work versus hype. Labels: "BROCHURE" above the left half, "LAB NOTEBOOK" above the right half.

key: Reading code vs debugging it.
name: ch00_reading_vs_debugging_code
alt: A developer skimming printed code once looks blank, while the same developer later traces a request through the system with sticky notes, a test and a calendar a week on.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same young software engineer (late 20s, round glasses, grey T-shirt, beard stubble) in a small Bengaluru office. LEFT panel: he leans back in his chair holding a long printout of code that drapes to the floor, eyes glazed, a blank expression and a little cloud of question marks over his head; the monitor behind him shows nothing open. RIGHT panel: the same man leans forward, sleeves pushed up, fully engaged. His monitor shows a debugger with a highlighted line, and a whiteboard beside him carries a hand-drawn path of boxes joined by a red marker arrow, a request travelling from box to box, with sticky notes stuck at each stop. On the desk, a mug, a notebook with a small test written out, and a green tick next to it. A wall calendar behind him has today circled and a second circle a week later with a small arrow, showing he came back. A faint glow of understanding surrounds his head. Lighting: left side flat and dull, right side warm with screen light and late-afternoon sun through a window. Mood: from passive to hands-on. Labels: "READ" at the top of the left panel, "TRACE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A music student is told to explain
name: ch01_music_student_every_note
alt: A music teacher points at a single note on a score while a student at the harmonium listens hard and explains why it is there.
scene: A warm interior of a small music classroom in an old Indian house, with a harmonium on a cotton durrie, a tanpura leaning against the wall and framed photos of instruments. In the foreground, a teenage girl (about 15, school uniform, two plaits) sits cross-legged at the harmonium, eyes half closed, head tilted, really listening, one finger hovering over a single key. Beside her, an elderly music teacher (white kurta, shawl over one shoulder, reading glasses pushed onto his forehead) holds a long sheet of handwritten notation and taps one small note on it with a pencil, his eyebrows raised in a question. The sheet in his hand is large enough to see: most notes plain, a few circled in red, a couple marked with a small shrug symbol meaning just filler. A speech bubble from the teacher contains only a big question mark next to a single note symbol. Behind them, a blackboard lists a row of notes, each with a tiny tick or a dash beside it, showing the drill of asking about every one. Faint sound waves curl from the harmonium toward the girl's ear. Lighting: soft afternoon sun through a barred window, dust in the light. Mood: patient, focused training of attention. Labels: "WHY THIS NOTE?" on the blackboard, "LISTEN" near the girl's ear.

key: The workbook is the gym; the 2012 book
name: ch01_gym_and_bus_textbook
alt: A young man trains at a gym with a workbook clipboard, and in a second scene reads the matching textbook on a city bus.
scene: A split-panel illustration showing the same young man (mid 20s, short hair, sports T-shirt, a small towel round his neck) in two places. LEFT panel: inside a busy neighbourhood gym with iron plates, mirrors and a rope on the floor, he is mid-squat with a barbell on his shoulders, face straining but determined. Clipped to a nearby rack is a thick spiral workbook open to a page of exercises with boxes ticked off. A trainer in a vest stands behind him, spotting, giving a thumbs-up. RIGHT panel: the same man, now in a collared shirt with a backpack, sits by the window of a crowded city bus, a commuter strap swinging above him, reading a thick textbook with a calm, curious face. The open page shows a small diagram of a muscle and a lever, the reason behind the exercise. Other passengers doze or look at phones. A dotted arrow runs from the diagram in the book across the divider to the barbell in the gym, linking the explanation to the effort. Lighting: the gym is bright and sweaty under tube lights; the bus is soft morning light through a dusty window. Mood: doing versus understanding, both useful. Labels: "WORKBOOK" on the clipboard, "TEXTBOOK" on the book's cover.

key: Learning to swim from a book versus
name: ch01_swim_book_vs_water
alt: A man who has memorised a swimming manual panics in deep water while a weathered swimmer floats calmly nearby.
scene: A split-panel illustration around a public swimming pool. LEFT panel: on a poolside bench, a young man (about 25, neat hair, spectacles, dry shorts and a T-shirt) sits reading a thick swimming manual with diagrams of arm strokes; he mimics a breaststroke in the air with confident hands, smiling, a thought bubble full of perfect stroke diagrams. RIGHT panel: the same man, now in the deep end of the pool with a sign on the tiled wall reading "3 m", is splashing in panic, eyes wide, mouth gasping, one hand reaching for the pool edge, the manual floating soggy beside him. A few metres away, an older woman swimmer (about 50, swimming cap, goggles pushed up, sun-darkened shoulders) floats calmly on her back, relaxed, as if resting on a sofa, years of water time showing in her ease. Small calendar pages drift in the air above her to show many years spent in the pool. Lighting: bright midday sun, glittering blue water, sharp shadows. Mood: the gap between knowing and being able. Labels: "BOOK" at the top of the left panel, "WATER" at the top of the right panel.

key: first month: red or white. After years
name: ch01_wine_taster_library
alt: A novice taster can only tell red from white, while years later the same taster draws on a vast mental library of past tastes for each sip.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a tasting room of a vineyard in the hills, wooden barrels stacked behind, rows of vines visible through an arched window. LEFT panel: a young woman taster (early 20s, apron over a plain blouse, hair in a ponytail) holds a glass and sniffs with an uncertain face. A small thought bubble above her head contains only two jars, one red and one pale gold. RIGHT panel: the same woman, years older (mid 40s, a few grey strands, reading glasses on a chain, same apron now stained), swirls a glass with quiet confidence. Her thought bubble is now a large library with tall wooden shelves holding hundreds of tiny labelled bottles; a ladder leans against it and one small bottle glows, the match for what she is tasting. A small notebook in her other hand shows rows of neat notes. The same glass and the same tongue are shown in both panels, emphasised by a small pink tongue icon in each corner. Lighting: warm golden late-afternoon light through the arched window, soft and reflective. Mood: experience as an expanding memory. Labels: "MONTH 1" at the top of the left panel, "YEAR 20" at the top of the right panel, "LIBRARY" on the shelves.

key: Motivation is a phone battery.
name: ch01_phone_battery_motivation
alt: A commuter holds a phone whose battery icon is draining, a glowing reason to carry it shown as a family photo, and a low-power mode switch that keeps routine tasks running.
scene: A close, slightly low-angle view of a young woman (late 20s, office kurta, sling bag, earphones) standing on a crowded suburban railway platform in the evening, holding a giant smartphone toward the viewer. The phone screen shows three things arranged top to bottom. At the top, a large battery icon draining from full to a thin red sliver, with tiny lightning bolts escaping each time a pop-up decision bubble appears beside it asking small questions like what to do now. In the middle, the lock-screen wallpaper: a glowing family photo of her parents and a little brother, showing why she carries the phone at all. At the bottom, a toggle switch flipped on, with a small leaf icon, and below it a short to-do list being ticked automatically, one item after another, while the battery drain slows to a trickle. Behind her, a train pulls in with its headlight on, and other commuters look tired. Her face is calm and steady despite the low battery. Lighting: yellow platform lamps, dusk-blue sky. Mood: steady routine beats bursts of willpower. Labels: "MOTIVATION" next to the battery, "VISION" next to the photo, "HABITS" next to the toggle.

key: Counting hours to judge learning
name: ch01_taxi_vs_racing_driver
alt: A veteran taxi driver with a huge odometer reading sits in traffic beside a young racing driver taking a sharp bend at speed.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a city street jammed with traffic, buses and autos, where an older taxi driver (about 60, grey moustache, khaki uniform shirt, towel over his shoulder) sits relaxed behind the wheel of a black-and-yellow taxi with one elbow out of the window, chewing on something, entirely at ease. A giant dashboard odometer floats above the taxi showing a huge number of kilometres with many digits, and a pile of twenty worn calendars is stacked on the roof rack. RIGHT panel: a racing circuit with red-and-white kerbs, where a young racing driver (late 20s, fireproof suit, helmet visor up, intense focused eyes) leans a sleek racing car hard into a sharp hairpin bend, tyres smoking, inches from the kerb, with a coach in a headset watching from the pit wall holding a stopwatch. Her small odometer reads far fewer kilometres. A large balance scale sits on the dividing line between the panels: the heavy odometer pile weighs down one pan labelled with kilometres, but a trophy sits on the other pan. Lighting: left side hazy grey city afternoon, right side sharp bright track light. Mood: quantity is not quality. Labels: "KM DRIVEN" above the taxi, "SKILL" above the racing car.

key: Practice is the tide raising every boat
name: ch01_tide_and_waves_boats
alt: A row of fishing boats in a harbour all rise slowly with the tide, while waves rock them so that on any one day a different boat sits highest.
scene: A wide side-on view of a small fishing harbour on the Konkan coast in late afternoon, like a cutaway where you can see the water level against a tall stone harbour wall marked with painted measuring lines. Five colourful wooden fishing boats float in a row, each with a fisherman aboard (different ages, lungis and vests, one with a cap). A long, gentle arrow on the harbour wall shows the tide line having risen steadily from a low mark up to a much higher mark, and all five boats sit higher than they did, shown by faint ghost outlines of the boats lower down. On top of that rise, choppy little waves pass under the boats, so one boat is lifted on a crest while its neighbour sits in a trough; one fisherman grins at being highest for the moment while another frowns. A small inset bubble in the corner shows the same row of boats on a different day, with a different boat on the crest. Gulls wheel overhead and nets are piled on the jetty. Lighting: warm low sun, glittering water, long shadows. Mood: the slow rise is real, the day-to-day order is luck. Labels: "TIDE" beside the long arrow on the wall, "WAVES" over the choppy crests.

key: Writing a summary of a lecture by hand
name: ch01_handwritten_notes_vs_recording
alt: In a coaching class one student records the lecture on a phone and stares blankly, while another writes short handwritten notes, choosing what matters.
scene: A view from the back corner of a crowded Indian coaching class: rows of wooden benches, a ceiling fan, a teacher in a sleeveless sweater writing on a green chalkboard covered with diagrams and arrows. In the foreground, two students sit side by side on the same bench. On the LEFT, a boy (about 18, hoodie, earbuds) has propped his phone against a water bottle with a red record dot glowing, recording everything; he slouches, eyes drifting to the window, his notebook empty. A huge cloud of sound waves flows into the phone, but a nearly empty thought bubble floats above his head. On the RIGHT, a girl (about 18, school cardigan, hair in a plait) leans forward over her notebook, pen moving, writing a few short lines with arrows and one underlined phrase; she pauses with the pen raised, frowning slightly, deciding. From the chalkboard, many words fly toward her like birds, and a small funnel sketched above her notebook lets only three through onto the page. Her thought bubble is small but full and glowing. Lighting: tube lights and a dusty shaft of late sunlight from the window. Mood: choosing is the learning. Labels: "REC" beside the phone, "NOTES" above the girl's notebook.

key: You know a cat can jump onto a table
name: ch01_cat_jump_table_not_roof
alt: A cat crouches in a courtyard, with a dotted arc showing it can reach a table but a much longer arc to the roof crossed out.
scene: A side view of the courtyard of an old Indian house: a whitewashed wall, a tiled roof high above, clothes drying on a line, a potted tulsi plant and a wooden table with a steel plate of fish on it. A ginger cat crouches on the floor, tail twitching, eyes fixed on the plate, haunches ready. A neat dotted arc rises from the cat to the table top and lands with a small green tick. A much longer dotted arc tries to climb to the edge of the roof, falls short halfway, and is crossed out with a red cross. On a cane chair nearby sits an old grandmother (white sari, glasses, a newspaper on her lap), glancing at the cat with a knowing half-smile, without any tape measure or tools; a thought bubble above her shows faint memories of many cats jumping onto many tables, like a stack of postcards. A young grandson beside her points at the roof, wide-eyed, and she shakes her head gently. Lighting: bright mid-morning sun with sharp shadows across the courtyard floor. Mood: everyday intuition sized by experience. Labels: "TABLE" next to the green tick, "ROOF" next to the red cross.

key: A ball rolling down a valley side
name: ch01_ball_valley_band
alt: A ball rolls down one side of a grassy valley and up the other, coming to rest somewhere inside a wide shaded band rather than on a single painted line.
scene: A wide side-on view of a smooth grassy valley between two green hills in the Western Ghats, with a few trees and a distant waterfall. A red cricket ball has rolled from the top of the left slope, down through the bottom, and up the right slope; its path is drawn as a dotted line with small ghost balls at intervals. On the right slope, a wide translucent yellow band is painted across the grass from roughly a third of the way up to about two thirds of the way up, and several faint ghost balls from earlier rolls have stopped at different places within it, scattered, none on the same spot. A single thin red line drawn across the slope at one exact height carries a small red cross next to it, while the wide band carries a green tick. In the foreground, two boys in school uniform crouch on the grass: one holds a ruler toward the slope with a puzzled face, the other spreads his arms wide as if to say roughly here, grinning. Lighting: soft late-afternoon light with long shadows, monsoon-green colours. Mood: rough zones beat precise lines. Labels: "ZONE" on the yellow band, "NOT A LINE" near the thin red line.

key: A staircase. Going up, each step
name: ch02_staircase_landing_doubt
alt: A man climbs a staircase whose steps and landings each rise higher, then pauses where one step is lower, unsure whether he is still climbing.
scene: A side cutaway of a long, irregular stone staircase built up a hillside temple path, drawn like a profile so every step top and every landing is clear. On the left, the stairs rise cleanly: each step's top is higher than the last and each flat landing is higher than the previous landing, with small green upward arrows marking both. A pilgrim (middle-aged man, white dhoti, orange shawl, a brass pot in one hand) climbs confidently here. In the middle, the staircase breaks its pattern: one step's top is lower than the one before it, marked by a small amber arrow, and the man stands still on a wide flat landing, scratching his head, looking both up and down the path, a question mark above him. Further right, faintly drawn in grey as a possible future, the path shows both a lower top and a lower landing, with two red downward arrows side by side, and a small sign post there. Monkeys sit on the side railing watching him. Lighting: early morning haze, soft golden sun behind the hill. Mood: steady progress, then a pause of honest doubt. Labels: "UP" over the clean rising section, "LANDING" over the flat middle, "DOWN" over the grey right section.

key: Learning to read a new script.
name: ch02_learning_new_script
alt: A girl sounds out letters one by one on a slate, and two weeks later reads whole words of a storybook at a glance.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same girl (about 7, school pinafore, two ribbons in her hair) in a small village school with a slate board and a painted alphabet chart on the wall. LEFT panel: she sits on a mat with a slate on her lap, tongue poking out in concentration, pointing with a chalk stick at one big letter of a new script; above her head the letters float separately with little sound bubbles under each, and a teacher (young woman in a cotton sari) kneels beside her, mouthing the sound. A wall calendar shows day one circled. RIGHT panel: the same girl sits on a bench, leaning back comfortably, reading a picture storybook; whole words float out of the book as single shapes rather than separate letters, and she is smiling at the story. The calendar now shows two weeks later circled. On the floor beside her bench lies a tall stack of letter drill sheets, untouched and gathering a little dust, with a small sleeping cat on top, showing that more drills now add little. Lighting: warm morning light through a window with wooden shutters. Mood: from effortful decoding to fluent reading. Labels: "LETTER BY LETTER" at the top of the left panel, "AT A GLANCE" at the top of the right panel.

key: Copying a map by hand versus glancing
name: ch02_copying_map_by_hand
alt: One student glances at a photo of a map on a phone, while another traces a river map by hand and knows every bend.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a school library with long wooden tables and a large framed river map of a region on the wall. LEFT panel: a teenage boy (about 15, school uniform, untucked shirt) holds up his phone and snaps a photo of the wall map, then turns away already scrolling something else; a thought bubble above his head holds only a blurry grey rectangle. RIGHT panel: a teenage girl (about 15, same uniform, spectacles) sits with a sheet of tracing paper over a printed map, carefully drawing a river with a fine pencil, her tongue between her teeth, an eraser and a sharpener beside her. Her drawing shows every bend of the river, a small tributary joining, a town dot and a bridge. Small numbered circles mark the places her pencil slowed down at the bends. Her thought bubble holds a crisp, detailed copy of the river with each bend glowing. A teacher in the background (older man, half-sleeve shirt, register under his arm) smiles approvingly at the girl. Lighting: soft daylight from tall windows, dust motes, quiet library mood. Mood: slow drawing beats quick glancing. Labels: "PHOTO" at the top of the left panel, "DRAWN" at the top of the right panel.

key: A runner on a long climb. Early on
name: ch02_runner_leaving_rest
alt: A runner on a long uphill road springs away from an early rest stop at full pace, but from a later rest stop takes two strides and slows to a walk.
scene: A wide panoramic side view of a long mountain road winding upward in the hills of Himachal, with pine trees and distant snow peaks. The same runner appears twice along the road. Lower down, on the left, at a small roadside water stall with a plastic chair and steel jug, the runner (woman in her 30s, running vest with a race number, cap, wristband) explodes away from the stall at full speed, arms pumping, long stride, a burst of motion lines behind her and dust kicked up. Higher up, on the right, near a second identical water stall closer to the top, the same runner leaves the stall with just two strides of running, shown by two footprints far apart, then the footprints shorten into small walking steps; she is bent forward, hands on hips, cheeks flushed, sweat on her brow. A volunteer at the higher stall (young man in a bright bib) watches with a knowing look. No one needs to ask her how she feels; the footprints tell it. Lighting: clear bright morning low on the road, slightly hazier and later toward the top. Mood: tiredness revealed by how she leaves each rest. Labels: "EARLY" by the lower stall, "LATE" by the higher stall.

key: A river (trend) that flows into a lake
name: ch03_river_lake_mouths
alt: An aerial view of a river flowing into a calm lake and out through a new river, with the murky mouths shaded as the hard-to-read zones.
scene: A high aerial view, like from a hill-top, of a landscape where a fast river enters from the left, widens into a broad calm lake in the centre and leaves through a new river on the far right, curving off in a different direction. The river sections show clear current lines and a small wooden boat with a boatman rowing easily downstream. The middle of the lake is glassy, with a fisherman sitting still in a coracle and lotus leaves around him, everything easy to read. The two places where river meets lake, the inflow mouth and the outflow mouth, are shaded with translucent grey patches; inside them the water swirls with small eddies and reeds, and a puzzled young boatman (about 20, vest and lungi, oar raised) has stopped his boat in the left mouth, looking around, a question mark above him, unsure whether the slowdown is the lake starting or just an eddy. Small curved arrows inside the shaded areas point in mixed directions. Birds fly over the lake. Lighting: soft morning light, mist hanging over the shaded mouths only. Mood: clarity in the middle, uncertainty at the edges. Labels: "RIVER" on the left channel, "LAKE" on the open water, "MOUTH" on the shaded inflow area.

key: Reading a mystery novel one page
name: ch03_mystery_novel_covered_page
alt: A reader of a detective novel covers the next page with her hand and writes down a suspect, while another reader skips to the ending first.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a cosy reading nook with a window seat and a cup of tea. LEFT panel: a young woman (late 20s, oversized cardigan, hair in a loose bun) holds a paperback detective novel open, her left hand firmly pressed over the right-hand page so she cannot see it. On a small notepad on her knee she has written a suspect's name and circled it, with three tiny clue sketches beside it: a footprint, a broken watch, a teacup. Her face is serious and committed. A faint pinboard of clues floats behind her head. RIGHT panel: a young man (late 20s, glasses, T-shirt) flips the same novel straight to the final page, reads the answer with a smug grin, then turns back to the start and points at a clue as if he had known it all along. A tiny ghost image of the last page hovers over his head with an arrow looping back to the first page, showing the cheat. Lighting: warm lamp light on the left, the same lamp on the right but with a mischievous glint. Mood: honest prediction versus hindsight. Labels: "COVERED" over the hand on the page, "PEEKED" over the man's book.

key: A staircase that turns into a ramp.
name: ch03_staircase_turns_ramp
alt: A staircase with landings where people step on turns into a smooth steep ramp with no landings, which ends at a sudden drop.
scene: A side cutaway of a large structure in an amusement park, read left to right. On the left, a normal staircase rises in clear flights with flat landings between them; at each landing a person steps on from the side with ease: a father holding a child's hand, a teenager, an older woman with a handbag, each with a small green arrow showing where they joined. In the middle, the steps melt into a smooth, glossy, steepening ramp, like a slide in reverse, with no landings at all. A young man (early 20s, sneakers, cap) runs alongside the ramp trying to jump on, arms flailing, finding nothing to stand on; a small red cross marks each spot he tries. Small figures already on the ramp glide upward fast, cheering. At the far right, the ramp ends abruptly at a cliff-edge with no railing and a sudden vertical drop, where a few figures are tumbling off into a pile of cushions far below, mouths open in surprise. Lighting: bright sunny day, colourful flags, long shadows. Mood: excitement with a hidden edge. Labels: "STAIRS" over the left section, "RAMP" over the glossy section, "DROP" at the cliff edge.

key: A recipe with twelve spices that only
name: ch03_twelve_spice_recipe
alt: A cook's twelve-spice dish succeeds only in its original kitchen, while a three-ingredient dish tastes good in several different kitchens.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: in one small, very particular kitchen with a specific old blue gas stove and a copper pot, a fussy chef (middle-aged man, white chef's cap, thin moustache, apron) carefully measures from a spice box of twelve tiny bowls, each one with a tiny dial set to an exact amount. His curry tastes perfect here: a happy diner gives a thumbs-up. Below, small inset bubbles show the same recipe cooked in three other kitchens, a hostel mess, a modern flat, a roadside dhaba, and in each the diner grimaces, with wavy stink lines. RIGHT panel: a relaxed home cook (woman in her 50s, cotton sari, bangles) uses just three simple ingredients, a tomato, an onion and a handful of salt, in an ordinary pan. Her inset bubbles show the same three-kitchen test, and in each the diner smiles. Tiny tags hang off the twelve spice bowls on the left, each one tied by a thin string to the old blue stove, showing they were tuned to that one kitchen. Lighting: warm kitchen glow with steam. Mood: simple and robust beats complex and fragile. Labels: "12 SPICES" above the left chef, "3 INGREDIENTS" above the right cook.

key: A tool belt with four tools.
name: ch03_tool_belt_hammer_only
alt: A carpenter with a four-tool belt picks the right tool for each job, while another carpenter with only a hammer waits for a nail to appear.
scene: A wide view of a busy carpentry workshop with wood shavings on the floor, a half-built wooden cupboard and planks leaning on the wall. On the left, an experienced carpenter (about 45, sleeveless vest, pencil behind his ear, measuring tape at his hip) wears a leather tool belt with exactly four tools in labelled pockets: a hammer, a saw, a screwdriver and a plane. He is choosing the saw for a plank on his bench, glancing at the job before reaching for the tool. Above the belt, four small icons float, each tool paired with its job: nail, plank, screw, rough edge, and each also with a small warning sign of how it goes wrong, a bent nail, a crooked cut, a stripped screw, a gouge. On the right, a second carpenter (younger, about 25, cap on backwards) holds only a gleaming hammer and is excellent with it: three perfectly sunk nails sit in a beam beside him. But now he sits on an upturned crate, chin on his hand, waiting, while screws and planks lie untouched next to him and a clock on the wall ticks. Lighting: dusty sunbeams through a high window. Mood: know which tool you are holding. Labels: "TOOL BELT" on the belt, "HAMMER ONLY" above the waiting carpenter.

key: A ball on a road between two hills.
name: ch03_ball_spring_and_slope
alt: A ball sits on a road in a dip between two hills, tied to a spring that pulls it toward the middle while a downhill slope tries to make it roll away.
scene: A side-on diagram-like scene of a road running through a shallow dip between two rounded green hills, with a few trees and a small roadside temple. A big red ball sits on the road. A large coiled metal spring connects the ball to a post planted at the exact middle of the dip; when the ball moves away, the spring stretches and pulls it back, shown by a curved arrow pointing toward the post. On one side of the ball, the road tilts downhill, and a second set of motion lines shows the ball wanting to roll faster and faster down that slope. Three small inset bubbles run along the bottom. In the first, the spring is thick and strong and the slope gentle: the ball snaps back to the middle. In the second, the slope is steep and the spring thin: the ball rolls away, picking up speed. In the third, the two are evenly matched: the ball just jiggles in place, shown by tiny wobbly lines, and a bored boy (about 10, shorts, kite in hand) yawns beside it. A small coin icon glows only over the first two insets, never the third. Lighting: clear afternoon, soft shadows. Mood: forces tugging in opposite directions. Labels: "SPRING" next to the coil, "SLOPE" along the tilted road.

key: A daily commute you know by heart.
name: ch03_commute_jolt_not_normal
alt: A daily commuter on autopilot is suddenly jolted awake by a closed lane and traffic moving unusually fast.
scene: A split-panel illustration seen through the windscreen and side window of a scooter rider's view on a familiar city road. LEFT panel: an office worker (man about 35, helmet, formal shirt, laptop bag strapped behind) rides his scooter along a road he knows by heart, eyes half-glazed, humming, a thought bubble about lunch; the scenery repeats with familiar landmarks, a chai stall, a bus stop, a big banyan tree, all slightly faded because he no longer notices them. A row of identical calendar pages floats in the sky, each showing the same road. RIGHT panel: the same man on the same road, but now his eyes are wide and his eyebrows shot up. A row of orange barricades closes one lane with a sign reading "CLOSED", and the cars beside him zoom past twice as fast as usual, with strong speed lines. A lightning-bolt jolt symbol crackles over his helmet, and the familiar landmarks suddenly appear vivid and sharp. A small inset in the corner shows a ghost of his usual quiet road, the memory that makes the change stand out. Lighting: hazy morning in the left panel; the same light but sharper, higher contrast in the right. Mood: only knowing normal lets you feel abnormal. Labels: "NORMAL" at the top of the left panel, "JOLT" at the top of the right panel.

key: A flight recorder has two tracks
name: ch04_flight_recorder_two_tracks
alt: Investigators study a flight recorder with two tracks, one showing the plane's instrument readings and the other the crew's voices, to tell a mechanical failure from a pilot error.
scene: A clean, brightly lit investigation lab with a long white table. In the centre sits a battered orange flight recorder box, its casing scratched and slightly scorched. Two thick cables run out of it to two screens, one on the left and one on the right. The LEFT screen shows lines of instrument readings: altitude, speed and engine dials drawn as simple wavy traces with one sudden dip circled in red. The RIGHT screen shows a sound waveform of voices with small speech bubbles above it, one calm, one hurried, one with an exclamation mark, lined up in time with the dip on the left screen by a vertical dotted line that crosses both screens. Two investigators stand at the table: a woman in her 40s with short grey hair, rolled-up sleeves and a lanyard, pointing at where the two tracks meet; and a younger man in his 30s with headphones round his neck, taking notes on a clipboard. On the wall behind them, a whiteboard has two columns with a question mark between them: a wrench icon on one side and a pilot's cap icon on the other. Lighting: cool white lab light, focused. Mood: careful cross-checking. Labels: "INSTRUMENTS" above the left screen, "VOICE" above the right screen.

key: Phase 1 is emptying a drawer onto
name: ch04_empty_then_sort_drawer
alt: A man first tips an entire drawer onto the floor, then sorts the heap into four labelled piles, beside a ghost image of a half-emptied drawer when sorting is done too early.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a cluttered bedroom with a wooden chest of drawers. LEFT panel: a man in his 30s (vest, track pants, reading glasses on his head) tips an entire drawer upside down onto a bedsheet spread on the floor, with an avalanche of objects tumbling out: cables, old phones, keys, receipts, a torch, rubber bands, a broken watch, coins. His face is cheerful and determined, not judging anything yet. RIGHT panel: the same man sits cross-legged in front of the heap, now sorting it into four clear piles on the bedsheet, each with a hand-written cardboard sign: a neat keep pile, a fix pile with a screwdriver beside it, a throw-away bin, and a wrong-drawer box. A small inset bubble in the top corner of the right panel shows the wrong way: a ghost version of him sorting while still pulling items out, with the drawer only half emptied and items left stuck at the back, marked with a red cross. Lighting: bright morning light through a window with a lace curtain. Mood: methodical, satisfying tidying. Labels: "EMPTY" at the top of the left panel, "SORT" at the top of the right panel.

key: Strength is a runner finishing a fast
name: ch04_strong_lap_vs_exhausted_sprint
alt: One runner finishes a fast lap with breath to spare, while a marathon runner throws everything into a final sprint and collapses after the line.
scene: A split-panel illustration at an athletics stadium with a red running track and stands. LEFT panel: a young male runner (about 22, vest and shorts, bib number) crosses a lap marker on the track at a fast pace, but his face is relaxed, mouth closed, breathing easily; small calm breath puffs come from his nose and he is already looking ahead to the next lap. A small banner on the side reads "LAP 3". A coach at the trackside nods, holding a stopwatch. RIGHT panel: a woman marathon runner (about 30, cap, sweat-soaked singlet, race number) bursts through the finish tape at the end of a long race in a huge final sprint, motion lines everywhere, face twisted with effort, then in the same frame, a few steps past the line, she is shown collapsing onto the track, legs gone, volunteers rushing in with a foil blanket. A banner overhead reads "42 KM". In both panels, the size of the burst of speed lines is equally large, showing that both moves look big; the difference is only in what came before and what follows. Lighting: bright stadium afternoon. Mood: two similar bursts, very different meaning. Labels: "STRENGTH" at the top of the left panel, "EXHAUSTION" at the top of the right panel.

key: Taking half at 1R is like banking half
name: ch04_bank_half_winnings
alt: A smiling player hands half his chips to the cashier's window to be paid out, keeping the other half to play on.
scene: A view inside a gaming hall with a long polished counter and a brass-barred cashier's window on the right, and blurred tables with green felt in the background. In the foreground, a man in his 40s (open-collar shirt, sleeves rolled, wristwatch, a contented smile) stands at the cashier's window holding a tall stack of coloured chips. He is splitting the stack cleanly with one hand: half slides through the window to a cashier (young woman in a waistcoat), who counts out banknotes into a small envelope; the other half he keeps in his other hand, ready to walk back to the tables. A dotted arrow from the kept half points back toward the tables, and a second dotted arrow from the envelope points to his breast pocket where it will stay safe. Above him, two small thought bubbles: one shows a huge glittering jackpot pile faded and crossed lightly, the other shows him walking out the door with the envelope, smiling. Behind him, another player slumps at a table with no chips left, his empty hands spread. Lighting: warm amber lamps over the counter, darker room behind. Mood: calm, sensible banking. Labels: "BANKED" on the envelope, "PLAY ON" next to the kept chips.

key: Testing a fishing spot: you
name: ch04_fishing_spot_vs_random_casts
alt: A fisherman compares his favourite spot with random casts across the same lake, and in a fish-filled lake every spot catches plenty.
scene: A wide high view of a calm lake surrounded by hills, early morning. On a small rocky point on the left, an older fisherman (about 60, white vest, lungi folded at the knee, cap) sits proudly at his favourite spot with a bucket of fish beside him. Out on the lake, a young woman researcher (about 30, life jacket, clipboard, cap) in a small rowing boat casts the same rod at many random places, each marked by a small numbered buoy scattered across the water, and each buoy has a small fish count tag floating beside it. A tally sheet on her clipboard compares two columns, the favourite spot and the random buoys, with nearly equal marks. Under the surface, cut away like a cross-section, the whole lake is crammed with fish swimming everywhere, not only near the rocky point. A small inset bubble in the corner shows a second lake with very few fish, where the favourite spot and the random buoys both catch little. Lighting: soft dawn light, mist on the water, gentle reflections. Mood: comparing against a fair baseline. Labels: "MY SPOT" by the rocky point, "RANDOM" over the buoys.

key: A restaurant. The business plan is why
name: ch07_restaurant_three_documents
alt: A restaurant shown with three layers of paperwork: a framed business plan in the office, a rule board in the kitchen, and individual recipe cards at the cooking station.
scene: A cutaway view of a small family restaurant, like a dollhouse with the front wall removed, showing three rooms left to right. LEFT room: the owner's office, where a woman owner (about 50, reading glasses, crisp salwar suit) stands beside a framed document on the wall with a clock icon for opening hours and a green fire-exit symbol, and a ledger on her desk. MIDDLE room: the kitchen, with a big chalk rule board on the wall listing a few dishes, each with a small rupee pot beside it showing the spending limit, and a head chef (man in his 40s, white chef's coat, moustache) pointing at the board while briefing a young assistant. RIGHT room: the cooking station, where a brand-new young cook (about 19, apron, nervous but focused) follows a single laminated recipe card clipped above the stove, with numbered steps and small pictures of each step, cooking a dish that matches the photo on the card exactly. Thin dotted arrows run from the framed plan to the rule board and from the rule board to the recipe card, showing each layer governs the next. Lighting: warm restaurant light, steam rising from pots. Mood: an orderly, well-run kitchen. Labels: "BUSINESS PLAN" on the framed document, "RULES" on the chalk board, "RECIPE" on the card.

key: A shop owner who has perfect recipes
name: ch07_recipes_but_no_shop
alt: A talented cook holds a binder of perfect recipes outside a shop with no opening hours, no accounts book and a fire extinguisher missing from its hook.
scene: A street-front view of a small eatery on a busy Indian market lane, early evening. A proud cook (man about 40, apron with flour on it, broad smile) stands in the doorway holding up a thick binder of beautiful recipe cards, each with a glossy photo of a perfect dish, fanned out like a winning hand. But all around him the shop is chaos. The signboard above the door is blank, with no name and no hours; a small hand-scribbled sheet taped on the shutter just says open sometimes with a question mark. Inside, a cash box lies open with notes stuffed in loosely and no ledger anywhere; a pile of unpaid bills spills off the counter. On the wall, an empty red hook and a faded outline show where a fire extinguisher should hang, while a pan on the stove smokes behind him. Customers on the street look at the shop, confused, and walk past to the neighbour's busy, well-signed stall. A dotted circle around the binder glows, while a dotted circle around the rest of the shop is dark. Lighting: orange evening street light, a few bulbs inside. Mood: great recipes, no business. Labels: "RECIPES" on the binder, "NO PLAN" on the blank signboard.

key: A sauce with fifteen ingredients and
name: ch07_spoiled_ingredient_sauce
alt: A taster frowns at a fifteen-ingredient sauce and cannot tell what is wrong, while a three-ingredient sauce lets another taster point straight at the one spoiled ingredient.
scene: A split-panel illustration on a restaurant kitchen counter. LEFT panel: a large pot of thick sauce surrounded by fifteen small bowls of ingredients, spices, herbs, pastes, nuts and oils, crowded together; one bowl in the middle has a faint greenish tinge and a tiny fly above it, but it is lost in the clutter. A cook (man about 35, white coat, cap) tastes from a wooden spoon with a puzzled, scrunched face, hand on his chin, a cloud of fifteen small question marks swirling over his head. RIGHT panel: a small pot of sauce with only three bowls beside it: tomatoes, garlic and a bowl of cream, the cream bowl visibly off with a sour curdled look and the same tiny fly. A second cook (woman about 30, white coat, hair net) tastes from her spoon and instantly points straight at the cream bowl with a confident face, a single exclamation mark above her head and a dotted arrow from her finger to the spoiled bowl. The remaining two bowls on the right glow slightly to show each ingredient must be excellent. Lighting: bright kitchen light, steam curling up from both pots. Mood: simplicity makes faults visible. Labels: "15" on the left pot, "3" on the right pot.

key: Nobody deploys straight from an idea
name: ch08_software_release_pipeline
alt: A software change travels along a pipeline from spec to tests to staging to production, with an incident sending a ticket back to the spec.
scene: A wide horizontal scene of a tech office drawn as a factory floor with a long conveyor belt running left to right through four booths. On the conveyor rides a small glowing cube representing a code change. Booth one, on the far left: a woman product engineer (early 30s, kurta, glasses) writes on a whiteboard covered with boxes and arrows. Booth two: a young tester (man about 24, hoodie, headphones) runs the cube through a row of small checking gates that flash green ticks. Booth three: a quieter replica room, a mock-up of a shop with dummy customers made of cardboard, where the cube is tried out safely while an engineer watches with a clipboard. Booth four, far right: a real bustling shopfront with real customers and a large live screen, where the cube is finally placed. Above booth four, a red siren light flashes and a paper ticket flies off on a long curved dotted arrow back over the whole conveyor to booth one, landing on the whiteboard. A small figure trying to throw a cube directly from booth one to booth four is blocked by a glass wall with a red cross. Lighting: clean office light. Mood: disciplined, staged release. Labels: "SPEC" over booth one, "STAGING" over booth three, "LIVE" over booth four.

key: Bar-by-bar testing is replaying a match
name: ch08_card_covering_future
alt: A cricket fan watches a match replay with a card covering the rest of the scorecard, writing down his prediction before sliding the card one step.
scene: A close, slightly over-the-shoulder view of a young man (mid 20s, cricket jersey, headband, pencil in hand) sitting at a small table in front of a long printed ball-by-ball scorecard of an old cricket match, spread across the table like a strip. A thick white card covers everything to the right of the current ball, so only the past is visible. His left hand is ready to slide the card one step to the right, shown by a small arrow on the card's edge. With his right hand he writes in a notebook beside the strip a short prediction, before revealing anything. The notebook shows a neat column of predictions with ticks and crosses filled in only for balls already revealed. On a TV behind him, a paused replay of a bowler in mid-delivery matches the visible ball. A small thought bubble shows a ghostly hand trying to lift the card's corner to peek, crossed out with a red cross. A steel cup of chai and a packet of biscuits sit next to the notebook. Lighting: warm table lamp, dim room, TV glow. Mood: patient, honest, no hindsight. Labels: "FUTURE" on the white card, "DECIDE" above the notebook.

key: Twenty traders, one rulebook, perfect
name: ch08_twenty_traders_same_rules
alt: Twenty traders follow the same rulebook at identical desks; one ends up signing copies of her own book while another sits with his head in his hands.
scene: A wide view of a large open trading room with twenty identical desks arranged in four neat rows, each desk with the same monitor, the same lamp and the same thick rulebook lying open at the same page. Each trader sits upright and disciplined, following the book. At the front of the room, a giant wall calendar shows a hundred pages torn off. In the foreground, two traders stand out. On the left, a woman (about 35, blazer, confident smile) stands on a small stage at a book launch, signing copies of a glossy hardback with her own face on the cover, a small crowd of admirers clapping. On the right, a man (about 35, rumpled shirt, loosened tie) sits at his desk with his head in his hands, staring at a downward line on his screen, crumpled papers around him. Thin dotted lines run from both of them back to the identical rulebook on their desks, showing they followed the same page. Above the room floats a large pair of dice, tumbling, casting a faint shadow over all twenty desks. Lighting: even office light, a spotlight on the stage. Mood: same rules, different luck. Labels: "SAME RULES" over the rows of desks, "LUCK" next to the dice.

key: A pilot flies by checklist and still
name: ch08_pilot_checklist_fences
alt: A pilot on approach reads a checklist that marks exactly where judgement is allowed, with a fenced zone on the approach path where a go-around decision is made.
scene: A view from just behind two pilots in the cockpit of a passenger plane on final approach, the runway lights visible ahead through the windscreen at dusk. The captain (woman in her 40s, crisp white shirt, epaulettes, headset) holds a laminated checklist card with one item highlighted in yellow and a small fence symbol drawn around it. The first officer (man in his 30s, headset, alert eyes) scans the instruments. Outside, projected onto the sky like an overlay, the approach path to the runway is drawn as a glowing corridor with a white picket fence running along both sides, and at one marked gate in the corridor a small decision sign is posted showing a fork: one arrow to land, one arrow curving back up into the sky. Within the fenced corridor, small gaps show room to make adjustments; outside the fences, the space is greyed out. A small inset bubble at the top shows the same crew on the ground before take-off, building the fence posts together with a mallet. Lighting: deep blue dusk with orange runway lights and green instrument glow. Mood: calm, prepared discretion. Labels: "CHECKLIST" on the card, "500 FT" at the decision gate.

key: The trend is the wind. You can stand
name: ch08_shouting_into_wind
alt: A confident man stands at the bow of a boat facing into a strong wind, and the spray, his hat and his papers blow straight back into his face.
scene: A dramatic side view of a wooden fishing boat with a lateen sail crossing a choppy bay under a big sky. A strong wind blows from right to left, shown by long sweeping white lines and the sail bulging hard. At the bow, a middle-aged man (about 45, crisp shirt, gold watch, chest puffed out, very sure of himself) stands with one foot on the gunwale, facing directly into the wind, one arm thrust forward, pouring a bucket of water forward into the wind with a bold expression. The water sprays straight back at him, drenching his face; his hat flies off behind him and sheets of paper from his shirt pocket whirl backwards around his head. Behind him, an old boatman (about 65, vest, towel on his head) calmly adjusts the sail to run with the wind, shaking his head with a small smile. A large curved arrow shows the water leaving the bucket forward and looping right back onto the man. Gulls glide easily with the wind above. Lighting: bright, windy afternoon, sparkling spray. Mood: confidence does not move the wind. Labels: "WIND" along the wind lines, "BACK AT YOU" next to the looping arrow.

key: Two scoreboards for the same predictions
name: ch08_two_scoreboards
alt: A TV pundit's scoreboard lists only his correct calls, while an account statement beside it lists every call including all the misses.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a bright TV studio with coloured lights, where a smug pundit (man about 50, shiny suit, slicked hair, pointing finger) stands in front of a giant scoreboard that shows only a column of large green ticks and a big glittering number of hits, with confetti falling. Beneath the scoreboard, half hidden behind the studio curtain, a large pile of crumpled red-crossed cards has been swept out of sight with a broom. RIGHT panel: a plain room with a desk and a desk lamp, where a quiet trader (woman about 35, cardigan, reading glasses) studies a long printed account statement unrolled over the desk and onto the floor, with every prediction listed in order, green ticks and red crosses mixed together, each with an amount, and a final total at the bottom underlined twice. A thin dotted line links the same prediction dates across both panels to show the same calls are counted. Lighting: left flashy studio spotlights, right a calm warm lamp. Mood: selective score versus honest score. Labels: "HITS ONLY" on the studio scoreboard, "EVERYTHING" on the account statement.

key: Learning to drive. The rules of the road
name: ch09_driving_rules_vs_calm
alt: A learner driver ticks off road rules on a neat weekly schedule, while staying calm when cut off on a highway has no fixed timetable at all.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a driving school yard with orange cones, a small practice car with an L plate and a wall chart showing a neat row of weekly boxes, each with a tick: signals, gears, parking, reversing. A young learner (woman about 22, kurta, dupatta tucked, hands at ten and two) drives slowly round the cones with a focused face, and an instructor (man about 50, white shirt, moustache, clipboard) sits beside her ticking the next box. RIGHT panel: a busy multi-lane highway at speed, where a truck suddenly swerves into her lane from the left, shown with sharp swerve lines. Three small versions of the same learner appear in three separate cars: one stays calm with steady hands, one grips the wheel white-knuckled with a shocked face, and one honks furiously with steam coming off her head. Above them hangs a calendar with pages flying off at different speeds, one at a month, one at many years, and no tick boxes at all. A dotted line from the tidy chart on the left stops abruptly at the panel border, showing the schedule cannot cross over. Lighting: calm morning on the left, harsh glaring midday on the right. Mood: teachable steps versus slow personal growth. Labels: "SKILLS" on the wall chart, "CALM" above the highway.

key: A photographer developing film.
name: ch09_film_print_sharpens
alt: In a red-lit darkroom a photographer returns to the same print day after day, and it sharpens a little each time from murky to clear.
scene: A cosy darkroom bathed in soft red safelight, with developing trays on a long bench, a wire line with clothes-pegs hanging across the room and a small enlarger in the corner. A photographer (woman about 40, sleeves rolled up, apron, hair tied back with a pencil through it) stands at the bench with tongs, lifting a print out of a tray and studying it with a patient half-smile. Along the drying line above her hang a row of prints of the same scene, a lighthouse on a rocky coast, pegged in order from left to right. The first print on the left is almost entirely murky grey with only a faint shape; each print to its right is a little sharper, the lighthouse slowly appearing, until the last print on the right is crisp, with the lighthouse, rocks and gulls clear. Under each print hangs a small paper tag with a day number. A small wall calendar near the door has many days ticked off. A stool and a cold cup of tea sit beside her, showing she keeps returning. Lighting: deep red glow, warm and quiet, faint white light leaking under the door. Mood: patient repetition reveals the picture. Labels: "DAY 1" under the first print, "WEEKS" under the last print.

key: A garden survey before you start weeding
name: ch09_garden_root_survey
alt: A gardener maps a garden bed before weeding, a cutaway showing how deep each plant's roots go and how much ground it covers, with the deep-rooted weed in the middle circled.
scene: A garden bed behind a village house drawn as a cutaway, showing both the plants above the soil and their roots below. A gardener (man about 55, cotton vest, gamchha on his shoulder, reading glasses on his nose) kneels at the edge of the bed with a clipboard, sketching a map rather than pulling anything; a trowel lies unused on the ground beside him. Above ground, plants of all kinds: a few small weeds, tomato plants on sticks, marigolds, a sprawling creeper. Below ground, the cutaway shows their roots: some short and shallow, some medium, and one tough weed in the very middle of the bed with a thick root plunging deep down and spreading wide sideways, crowding the vegetables. On his clipboard map, each plant is a circle whose size shows how much ground it covers and whose shading shows how deep its root goes; the big dark circle in the middle is ringed in red. A small dotted measuring tape runs down beside the deep root. In the background, a neighbour yanks plants at random in his own bed, leaving broken root stubs, with a red cross over him. Lighting: early morning sun, dew on leaves. Mood: survey first, act later. Labels: "DEPTH" beside the deep root, "SPREAD" across the wide root area.

key: A car and a driver. A calm, skilled
name: ch09_engine_and_driver
alt: A calm driver sits in a car with an empty engine bay going nowhere, while a powerful car with an erratic driver moves forward but dented and veering.
scene: A split-panel illustration on a long straight road through fields. LEFT panel: a vintage car with its bonnet propped open reveals a completely empty engine bay, just bare metal and a cobweb. In the driver's seat sits a calm, skilled driver (woman about 40, driving gloves, sunglasses, perfect posture), hands relaxed on the wheel, serene expression, but the car has not moved from the start line painted on the road; a small snail overtakes it. RIGHT panel: a powerful car with a gleaming, oversized engine visible through a cutaway bonnet races forward, well past the start line and far down the road. The driver (man about 30, cap askew, tense face) swerves now and then: the tyre tracks behind him zigzag and dip into a roadside ditch twice, and the car carries dents and a dangling bumper, but it is clearly further ahead. A small inset in the corner of the right panel shows the ideal: the same strong engine with the calm driver, far ahead and smooth. Lighting: bright countryside afternoon, dust in the air. Mood: edge first, then the driving. Labels: "NO ENGINE" over the left car, "ENGINE" over the right car.

key: A chess player reviewing a game.
name: ch09_chess_review_sound_moves
alt: A chess player reviews a finished game move by move, marking each move as sound or unsound rather than looking at who won.
scene: A quiet chess club room with wooden tables, chess clocks and a framed tournament poster on the wall. In the foreground, a young woman chess player (about 25, cardigan, hair tied, pen tucked behind her ear) sits alone after a game, the board still set with the final position. Instead of looking at the result slip lying face down at the edge of the table, she leans over a scoresheet listing every move in a column and marks each one with a small symbol: mostly green ticks, a couple of orange question marks and one red cross. Beside the board, a small floating set of ghost pieces replays one earlier move, with an arrow showing the alternative she should have played. Behind her, two small inset bubbles: in one, a sound game ends in a loss because the opponent got a lucky blunder, shown with a small lightning bolt; in the other, a game full of red crosses ends in a lucky win. Far in the background, a long shelf holds hundreds of filed scoresheets, and a rising stack of trophies stands at the end of it. Lighting: warm table lamp over the board, the rest of the room in soft shade. Mood: judge the process, not the result. Labels: "EACH MOVE" above the scoresheet, "RESULT" on the face-down slip.

key: People press it, the doors close a few
name: ch09_lift_button_not_wired
alt: Office workers jab a lift's close-door button whose wire is cut behind the panel, convinced it worked when the doors close on their own timer.
scene: The inside of a crowded office lift, seen from the back corner, with brushed steel walls and a panel of buttons by the door. A young man (about 28, formal shirt, ID lanyard, coffee cup) jabs the close-door button repeatedly with an impatient face. The panel is drawn as a partial cutaway showing the wiring behind it: every floor button has a neat coloured wire running away into the wall, but the close-door button's wire hangs loose and cut, ending in mid-air with a little spark-less end. Meanwhile, a separate small timer mechanism above the doors, a clock dial with a ticking hand, is shown connected to the doors by a thick cable; the doors are sliding shut, driven by the timer. A satisfied thought bubble above the young man shows the button glowing with a tick, as if he caused it. An older woman beside him (about 55, saree, handbag) smiles knowingly. Two other passengers nod at the young man approvingly. Lighting: cool fluorescent lift light, shiny reflections. Mood: false sense of control. Labels: "NOT WIRED" next to the cut wire, "TIMER" next to the clock dial.

key: A camera lens with smudges on it.
name: ch09_smudged_lens_wipe
alt: A photographer wipes a camera lens covered in smudges, each smudge holding a small memory, so the scene in front can be seen clearly.
scene: A close-up view of a large camera lens filling most of the frame, held by a photographer's hands (young man, about 30, wristband, plain T-shirt sleeve visible). On the glass of the lens are several greasy smudges, and inside each smudge a tiny faded memory picture is visible: a red downward arrow with a sad face, an old chart with a cross on it, a newspaper headline icon, a frowning man. Through the smudges, the scene beyond the lens, a busy morning market street, is blurred and distorted. The photographer is wiping the lens with a soft cloth in a circular motion; the half that has been wiped is crystal clear, and through it the market is sharp and bright, a vendor arranging fruit, a cyclist, a cow, real details of today. The wiped-off smudges are drawn drifting away from the cloth as small grey puffs. A small inset at the top shows the photographer's face behind the camera, calm and attentive. Lighting: crisp morning light on the clear half, dull and murky through the smudged half. Mood: clearing the past to see the present. Labels: "MEMORIES" on the smudged half, "TODAY" on the clear half.

key: Food that comes pre-salted.
name: ch09_pre_salted_news
alt: A man eats a plate of vegetables that come with salt already poured on, the salt spilling from a newspaper shaker into his worried mood.
scene: A dining-table scene in a small apartment kitchen, mid-morning. A man in his 40s (spectacles, cotton shirt, reading a folded newspaper in one hand) eats from a steel plate of fresh green vegetables with the other hand. Above the plate floats a giant salt shaker shaped like a rolled-up newspaper, already pouring a heavy stream of white salt onto every vegetable before he can stop it; he did not pick it up. Each salt grain has a tiny worried face or exclamation mark on it. A dotted arrow runs from the vegetables into his body, and a cutaway mood meter on his chest, drawn as a simple thermometer, rises toward a worried red zone. His face is tense, brow furrowed, even though the food itself is healthy. Beside the plate, a small bowl of plain unsalted vegetables sits untouched, with a small spoon, as a reminder of the fact without the emotion. Through a window behind him, a peaceful sunny day contrasts with his mood. Lighting: bright ordinary daylight, slightly harsh. Mood: facts come with feelings attached. Labels: "NEWS" on the shaker, "FEAR" on the thermometer's red zone.

key: A great hitter fails about two times
name: ch09_batter_strikeouts
alt: A batter stands at the plate, with a long trail of ghostly strikeouts behind him and a few home runs soaring away ahead.
scene: A wide view of a baseball diamond under evening stadium lights, seen from slightly behind home plate. A veteran batter (man about 35, grey uniform with a plain number, helmet, determined eyes) steps confidently into the batter's box, bat raised. Behind him, stretching back toward the dugout like a long queue, stand many faint translucent ghost versions of himself, each walking away dejected with the bat lowered after a strikeout, heads down. Ahead of him, above the outfield, a few bright arcs of baseballs fly over the fence into the night, each trailing a star, with a small cheering crowd in the stands. A simple tally board on the outfield wall shows two rows of small marks, many more in the strikeout row than in the hits row. A teammate in the dugout (younger man, cap, chewing gum) watches with admiration. The ghosts and the home-run arcs are both drawn connected to the same bat by thin dotted lines, showing both come from stepping up. Lighting: bright white stadium floodlights, dark blue sky. Mood: the misses are the price of the hits. Labels: "STRIKEOUTS" over the ghost queue, "HOME RUNS" over the arcs.

key: A smoke alarm. Ripping it off the wall
name: ch09_smoke_alarm_check_and_settle
alt: A woman hears the kitchen smoke alarm, checks whether there is a fire, finds burnt toast, and opens the window instead of ripping the alarm off or suffering it.
scene: A small apartment kitchen drawn as a comic-strip row of four panels from left to right, each separated by a thin line, with the same woman (about 35, cotton nightdress, hair in a messy bun, house slippers). Panel one: a round smoke alarm on the ceiling shrieks with zigzag sound lines; she covers her ears, startled. Panel two: she pauses, looks around the kitchen, sniffs the air and peers at the toaster, where two slices of toast are blackened with a thin curl of smoke; no flames anywhere. Panel three: she closes her eyes briefly and a small thought bubble above her shows the worst case, a big fire, which she calmly considers. Panel four: she opens the window wide, waves a tea towel gently under the alarm, and the sound lines shrink to nothing; she smiles, relaxed, the alarm still in place on the ceiling. Above the strip, two small crossed-out insets show the wrong choices: a man yanking the alarm off the ceiling with wires dangling, and a man huddled miserably with the alarm screaming for hours. Lighting: bright morning sun, a little haze of smoke in the first panels clearing by the last. Mood: listening to fear, then letting it settle. Labels: "CHECK" over panel two, "WORST CASE" over panel three, "SETTLE" over panel four.

key: A seesaw with return on one end
name: ch09_seesaw_return_vs_bad_year
alt: A seesaw in a playground has a bag of gold coins on one end and a storm cloud of bad years on the other, and a man tries to nail both ends up at once.
scene: A side view of a long wooden seesaw in a neighbourhood park, with swings and a banyan tree in the background. On the left end of the seesaw sits a sack of gold coins spilling over, and the left end is raised high in the air. On the right end sits a small dark storm cloud with a lightning bolt, and that end is pressed low to the ground. A clear curved double arrow over the pivot shows that as one end goes up, the other must go down. In the middle, standing on the pivot, a woman (about 30, sporty kurta, ponytail) holds onto the plank and chooses where to shift her weight, calmly. On the far right, a man (about 45, office shirt, tie loosened, frustrated face) kneels with a hammer and a box of nails, trying to nail both ends of the seesaw up at the same time; nails are bent and the plank is cracking, with a red cross above him. A small boy on the swings watches him, puzzled. A tiny sign stuck in the grass near the man shows a wish list with a big number and a crossed-out storm icon. Lighting: late-afternoon park light, long shadows. Mood: you can choose, but not both. Labels: "RETURN" on the gold end, "BAD YEAR" on the storm end.

key: someone has put a door in the wall
name: ch09_game_character_door_letter
alt: A cartoon video-game character runs toward a brick wall, but a door has been set into the wall with a sign telling him to stop, go outside and come back slowly.
scene: A side-scrolling video-game scene drawn like a retro platform game: blocky grass ground, puffy pixel clouds, a few coins floating in the air and a score counter at the top corner. A small round-headed game character (cartoonish, red cap, blue overalls, big shoes) runs at full speed from the left toward a tall red brick wall on the right; faint ghost copies of him behind show he has run into this wall many times before, each ghost with small dizzy stars over its head. But now a wooden door has been fitted into the brick wall, with a brass handle and a clear white sign pinned to it. The sign shows three small pictures in a row: a stop hand, a figure stepping out into a sunny garden, and a figure walking slowly back in. The character has just skidded to a stop in front of the door, dust puffing from his shoes, reading the sign with a surprised face. Through the half-open door, a calm sunny garden with a bench and a tree is visible. A dotted path loops from the door out into the garden and back, ending in slow footprints. Lighting: bright cheerful game colours, soft glow from the garden. Mood: a planned way out of the loop. Labels: "WALL" on the bricks, "THE LETTER" on the door.

key: tells, turned on yourself. You learn
name: ch09_own_tells_mirror
alt: A trader sees in a mirror that he taps the desk and has stopped writing in his journal, the warning signs that come just before he revenge trades.
scene: A home trading desk at night with two monitors glowing, a cold cup of tea and an open journal. A man in his 30s (crumpled T-shirt, stubble, headphones around his neck) sits at the desk, his right hand drumming fingers hard on the wood, shown with small tapping motion lines, while his left hand hovers near the mouse. The journal beside him has a neat entry at the top and then abruptly blank lines, with the pen dropped across the page. On the wall in front of him is a large mirror, and in the reflection, the scene is circled like a poker player studying an opponent: two red circles drawn on the mirror around the tapping fingers and the abandoned pen, with small exclamation marks. A small poker table inset in the corner of the mirror shows a card player across a table with the same tapping hand, the classic tell. A wall clock shows a minute hand pointing with a small arrow to one minute ahead, where a faint ghost of the man is lunging at the buy button. The man's eyes have just caught the reflection; he freezes. Lighting: blue monitor glow and a warm desk lamp. Mood: catching yourself early. Labels: "TAP" by the fingers, "NO JOURNAL" by the blank page.

key: Three layers like weather talk.
name: ch09_opinion_bias_action_weather
alt: Three people in a lane talk about the weather at three levels: one with a vague hunch, one with a weather map and a condition, and one simply opening an umbrella in the rain.
scene: A narrow lane in an Indian town during the monsoon, with balconies, hanging wires and puddles, drawn as one wide scene with three people standing left to right on three steps of a shop front. Left, lowest: an old man on a plastic chair (vest, lungi, newspaper fan) leans back and waves his hand vaguely, a cloud-shaped speech bubble holding a little sun icon with a shrug, his idle guess. His figure is drawn slightly faded, to be ignored. Middle step: a woman (about 35, raincoat over a salwar, clipboard) holds up a weather map with a big high-pressure symbol and a calendar page marking Thursday with a small cross that would mean she is wrong; she looks thoughtful and holds the map loosely between two fingers. Right, top step: a young man (about 25, school-teacher look, satchel) has just felt raindrops on his palm and is opening a black umbrella decisively, rain clearly falling around him right now. Three translucent hands of different firmness appear above each person: barely touching, lightly holding, firmly gripping. Lighting: grey monsoon light with a glint of wet surfaces. Mood: act on what is happening now. Labels: "OPINION" over the old man, "BIAS" over the woman, "ACTION" over the young man.

key: Learning to cook. In week one
name: ch09_omelette_tongue_better
alt: A beginner proudly loves his first lopsided omelette, while a year later the same cook frowns at a much better dish that his friends are enjoying.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a small bachelor flat kitchen with a two-burner stove. LEFT panel: a young man (about 23, vest and shorts, spatula in hand) holds up a lopsided, slightly burnt omelette on a plate, beaming with pride, eyes closed in delight, small hearts and stars floating above it. A tiny calendar on the fridge shows week one. A small cartoon tongue icon next to him has only two simple taste dots on it. RIGHT panel: a year later, the same man (now with a neat apron and a spice rack on the wall behind him) tastes from a spoon a well-plated, nicely browned omelette with herbs; his friends around the table (two young women and a young man) are happily eating and giving thumbs-up, but he frowns slightly, his eyebrows knitted, noticing small flaws: tiny labels hover over the dish pointing at too much salt and a slightly dry edge. His tongue icon now has many taste dots in different colours, a detailed map. The calendar on the fridge shows a year later. Lighting: warm evening kitchen light in both panels. Mood: the palate improved faster than the cooking. Labels: "WEEK 1" at the top of the left panel, "YEAR 1" at the top of the right panel.

key: Student pilots fly small planes
name: ch09_pilot_licence_ladder
alt: A student pilot progresses up a ladder of planes, from a small trainer with an instructor to solo flight to passengers, while a giant airliner sits far above out of reach.
scene: A wide view of a small flying-school airfield with a windsock, a hangar and green fields, arranged as a gently rising path of four stages from left to right. Stage one: a tiny two-seater trainer plane on the grass, with a student pilot (woman about 24, flight jacket, headset) in the left seat and an instructor (grey-haired man, sunglasses, clipboard) beside her pointing at a gauge. Stage two: the same small plane in the air under fair blue skies, now with only her inside, smiling nervously. Stage three: a slightly bigger plane, her logbook open on a step beside it with many hours entered and a small rating badge pinned to her jacket. Stage four: a four-seat plane with two passengers climbing in, waving, as she does her walk-around check with confidence. Far above, at the top right corner on a high platform reachable only by a long staircase, sits a huge airliner with many windows; at the bottom of that staircase a rope barrier is drawn, and an eager young man in a cap tries to rush up it while an official gently stops him. Lighting: clear bright morning, soft clouds. Mood: earning bigger planes step by step. Labels: "STUDENT" under stage one, "SOLO" under stage two, "PASSENGERS" under stage four.

key: A casino floor and a statistics
name: ch10_roulette_players_vs_statisticians
alt: Gamblers at a roulette wheel scribble notes about hot numbers while statisticians in a glass booth above see a wheel with no memory.
scene: A two-level cutaway scene.
