On the lower level, a glamorous gaming floor with chandeliers and a roulette table with green felt; four players crowd around it: an old man with a pencil and a notebook full of circled numbers, a young woman pointing excitedly at a streak of red results on the small result board, a man in a tuxedo whispering about a hot number, and a nervous student counting chips. Their notebooks and thought bubbles are full of arrows, streak patterns and lucky numbers. On the upper level, behind a glass wall overlooking the same wheel, sits a quiet office with whiteboards and coffee mugs: three statisticians (an older woman with silver hair and a cardigan, a young man with glasses, a middle-aged man with a beard) look down at the very same wheel. Their whiteboard shows a simple wheel diagram with a small brain symbol crossed out, meaning no memory, and a flat even row of bars. A big question mark hangs in the middle of the glass wall between the two levels, with a small market price line drawn inside it, the question of which view fits markets. Lighting: warm, gold casino glow below; cool, even office light above. Mood: two ways of seeing the same wheel. Labels: "PLAYERS" on the lower level, "NO MEMORY" on the whiteboard.

key: Testing a recipe by tasting the cake.
name: ch10_bad_cake_which_part
alt: A baker stares at a sunken cake surrounded by the recipe, the oven, the flour and the cook, each with a question mark, unable to tell which one failed.
scene: A home kitchen with a tiled counter, mid-afternoon. In the centre of the counter sits a sunken, lopsided cake on a plate, with a slice cut out showing a gooey middle. A woman baker (about 40, flour on her apron and cheek, hair tied up) stands behind it, tasting a forkful, grimacing, then staring at the cake with her hand on her hip. Around the cake, arranged in a ring and connected to it by thin dotted lines like the spokes of a wheel, are four suspects, each with a large question mark tag: an open recipe book on a stand, the oven with its door open and its dial shown, a sack of flour slumped on the floor, and a small mirror on the wall reflecting the baker herself as the cook. All four are tied together by one loop of kitchen string, so none can be tested alone. A small inset bubble in the corner shows a scientist holding up a sign with the theory written on it, also tied by the same string to a second sign labelled normal returns, showing they always come bundled together. Lighting: warm afternoon window light, a little steam rising. Mood: a failure that cannot point to its cause. Labels: "RECIPE" on the book, "OVEN" on the oven door.

key: Most days the market is a sleepy
name: ch10_sleepy_commute_and_pileup
alt: Most days a motorway is quieter than expected with a sleepy commute, but on a few days a sudden huge pile-up happens that the planners never expected.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same long motorway seen from a high overpass. LEFT panel, large: a calm early-morning motorway with sparse traffic, cars spaced evenly, a bus driver yawning, a man on a scooter sipping chai at a red light; it is even quieter than a planner's chart pinned to a lamp post expected, shown by a little smooth bell-shaped sign beside the road with a dashed line well above the actual traffic. A small calendar tag shows most days. RIGHT panel, narrower: the same motorway on a rare stormy day, with a massive pile-up of cars, trucks and buses jammed and crumpled together, flashing ambulance lights, a traffic police officer waving both arms; the same bell-shaped sign on the lamp post here shows a dashed line far below the chaos, the plan completely wrong. A small calendar tag shows a few days a year. Between the panels, a simple scale with a feather on one side (many sleepy days) and a boulder on the other (one pile-up) tips toward the boulder. Lighting: soft dawn light on the left, dark storm clouds and flashing lights on the right. Mood: mostly calm, occasionally catastrophic. Labels: "QUIET" at the top of the left panel, "PILE-UP" at the top of the right panel.

key: A drunk walking home down a slight
name: ch10_tipsy_walker_downhill
alt: A tipsy man zigzags randomly down a gently sloping lane at night and still ends up further downhill, while onlookers fail to predict his next step.
scene: A night scene of a long, gently sloping lane in an old town, cobbled, lit by a row of street lamps, with closed shop shutters and a sleeping dog. A tipsy man (about 45, loosened shirt, one chappal in his hand, a garland askew around his neck from a wedding) staggers down the lane. His path is drawn as a winding dotted zigzag line, lurching left and right, sometimes stepping back uphill, but overall drifting down the slope, ending much lower than where he began. A large tilt arrow painted along the ground shows the slope of the lane. On the side, two neighbours lean out of a window: one points to where he thinks the man will step next, clearly wrong, with a small red cross where the next footprint actually lands; the other just shrugs. At the bottom of the lane, a small boy holds a cardboard sign praising the walker's skill, and a grandmother beside him shakes her head and points at the slope instead. Small numbered footprints along the zigzag show steps one to twenty. Lighting: warm sodium street lamps, deep blue night sky, soft glow. Mood: random steps, tilted ground, no skill. Labels: "SLOPE" along the tilt arrow, "NEXT STEP?" near the neighbours.

key: A lottery winner on TV explaining
name: ch10_lottery_winner_interview
alt: A lottery winner explains his system on a TV show, while behind the studio a huge crowd of losing ticket holders with the same system is never interviewed.
scene: A TV studio set with bright lights and a glossy desk. A cheerful lottery winner (man about 50, new suit a size too big, gold chain, big grin) sits beside a smiling host (woman about 35, sequined top, microphone) and points to a whiteboard behind him covered with a complicated system of lucky numbers, circles, star signs and arrows. A giant cheque leans against the desk. A camera on a tripod in the foreground focuses only on him, with a narrow cone of light from the camera lens that captures just the winner. Outside the cone, through a big window at the back of the studio, a huge crowd of people stretches into the distance, each holding a torn lottery ticket and a notebook with the very same system scribbled on it, all looking glum and ignored. A security guard holds a velvet rope in front of them. A small dotted outline traces the cone from the camera to the winner only, making it clear the selection is the camera's choice. Lighting: hot studio spotlights on the winner, dim grey light on the crowd outside. Mood: we only hear from the winners. Labels: "MY SYSTEM" on the whiteboard, "NEVER INTERVIEWED" over the crowd.

key: She looks for where it bends most
name: ch10_engineer_bridge_bends
alt: A structural engineer inspects a long bridge under heavy traffic, marking the places where it bends most with red flags.
scene: A side view of a long steel truss bridge over a wide river, with a line of heavy trucks crossing it. Under the weight, the bridge deck sags slightly in several places, exaggerated so it is easy to see. A structural engineer (woman about 45, hard hat, reflective vest over a cotton shirt, binoculars round her neck) stands on a small inspection platform hanging under the bridge, holding a tablet and a strain gauge clipped to a beam. She is not trying to knock the bridge down: she is calmly marking each spot where it bends most with a small red flag; seven red flags are planted along the underside of the bridge, numbered one to seven. Small dotted curves show the bend at each flag. On the riverbank, a crowd of townspeople looks up at the bridge, and a small boy points at one of the flags. The bridge as a whole still stands firm, with traffic moving across. A tiny inset in the corner of the image shows her clipboard with seven boxes, each matching a flag. Lighting: clear morning light, glinting off the river and the steel. Mood: careful, honest inspection. Labels: "BENDS" beside the row of red flags, "BRIDGE" on the bridge's side.

key: A fire alarm in a building with two
name: ch10_exit_extt_doors
alt: A fire alarm sounds and people rush through a door marked with a misspelled exit sign before reading it, while the real exit is next to it.
scene: A busy office corridor during a fire alarm, red lights flashing and a ringing bell shown with zigzag sound lines. Two identical green doors stand side by side at the end of the corridor. Above the left door hangs a glowing sign reading "EXIT". Above the right door hangs a nearly identical sign reading "EXTT", one letter wrong. A crowd of office workers (a man with a laptop under his arm, a woman holding her shoes, a young intern with a coffee cup, an older peon in a khaki uniform) rushes down the corridor in a panic. Most of them pile into the right-hand door without looking up, pushing through; it opens into a broom cupboard full of mops and buckets, where the first few people have stopped, confused. Behind them, a few people have stopped to read the signs and are turning toward the correct left door. Small eyes-closed icons above the rushing people show they did not read the sign. A calm safety officer (woman about 40, reflective vest, whistle) stands at the side pointing at the correct door. Lighting: pulsing red alarm light, fluorescent tubes. Mood: panic outruns reading. Labels: "EXIT" above the left door, "EXTT" above the right door.

key: A stone dropped in a bath.
name: ch10_stone_in_bath_slosh
alt: A stone dropped into a full bathtub makes the water slosh over, fall back and slosh again before settling at a new, higher level.
scene: A side cutaway view of a white enamel bathtub filled with water in a tiled bathroom, drawn like a strip of four moments from left to right inside the same tub outline, with faint dividing lines. In the first moment, a hand (man's, with a wristwatch) drops a large smooth grey stone; a dashed line on the tub wall marks the original water level. In the second moment, the water surges up one end and sloshes over the rim onto the floor, well above where it will end up. In the third moment, the water rushes back and dips below the final level at that end, with a smaller slosh at the other end. In the fourth moment, the water lies flat and still at a new level, slightly higher than the original dashed line, marked with a second solid line. Above the strip, a neat inset bubble shows the ideal theory: a tub where the water jumps once to the new level and stays perfectly flat, drawn crisp and clean. A rubber duck bobs in every moment, tossed around in the middle two and calm at the end. A small boy in a towel peeks round the door, delighted by the splash. Lighting: bright white bathroom light, sparkling water. Mood: real adjustment is messy before it settles. Labels: "OVERSHOOT" over the second moment, "NEW LEVEL" by the final line.

key: A scoreboard that updates when the
name: ch10_scoreboard_before_whistle
alt: A stadium scoreboard already shows a goal while the referee has not yet blown his whistle and nobody in the crowd has seen anything.
scene: A wide view of a football stadium at night under floodlights. On the pitch, the ball has just crossed near the goal line amid a scramble of players; the referee (man about 40, black kit, whistle not yet at his lips) is only beginning to raise his arm, his face showing he has just decided. A thin glowing thought line runs from the referee's head straight up into the giant electronic scoreboard above the stands, which already flashes the updated score with a big bright one-goal change and fireworks graphics. In the stands, thousands of fans are still mid-gasp, looking at the goalmouth, unaware; a father with his son on his shoulders squints, uncertain. Nobody is cheering yet. A small clock icon near the referee and another near the scoreboard show that the scoreboard changed before the whistle. In one corner of the stands, a single fan is staring at the scoreboard, mouth open in shock that it already knows. Lighting: bright white floodlights, dark sky, the scoreboard glowing brightest of all. Mood: impossibly fast information. Labels: "SCOREBOARD" on the screen, "NO WHISTLE YET" near the referee.

key: A town where everyone trusts the weather
name: ch10_forecast_station_closed
alt: A small town trusts its weather forecast so much that the weather station is boarded up, and the next week the forecast board is blank.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same small hill town square. LEFT panel: a busy square with a large public forecast board on a pole showing tomorrow's sun-and-cloud symbols; townspeople (a vegetable seller, a schoolteacher with an umbrella tucked away, a farmer with a hoe) glance at it confidently and walk on. On a hill behind the square, a small white weather station with a spinning anemometer, a rain gauge and a man in a cap reading instruments is just visible. A town official in a Nehru jacket points at the board and waves dismissively at the station on the hill, a speech bubble showing the station with a cross. RIGHT panel: one week later, the same square. The weather station on the hill is boarded up with planks and a padlock, the anemometer still, cobwebs on the gauge. The forecast board in the square is completely blank, only a big question mark scrawled on it. Townspeople gather beneath it, confused, looking up at an uncertain grey sky; the official scratches his head. Lighting: bright sunny on the left, dull overcast on the right. Mood: trusting the answer kills the source of the answer. Labels: "STATION" on the hill building, "NO FORECAST" on the blank board.

key: A room where half the people are nodding
name: ch10_nodding_room_cancels
alt: In a meeting room half the people nod yes and half shake their heads no, and an overhead average meter shows zero movement.
scene: A wide view of a large meeting hall with rows of folding chairs, about twenty people seated, facing a speaker at a lectern with a microphone. Half the audience, scattered throughout, nod their heads up and down vigorously, drawn with vertical motion arcs and small green tick bubbles. The other half shake their heads side to side, drawn with horizontal motion arcs and small red cross bubbles. Every face is animated and every head is moving: a grandfather in a cap nodding, a college girl shaking her head, a shopkeeper nodding, a woman in a sari shaking hers. On the ceiling hangs a large old-fashioned dial meter connected by thin wires to every chair, and its needle sits exactly in the middle at zero, perfectly still, with a tiny sleeping face on it. A small inset beside the meter shows two arrows, one up and one down, adding to nothing. The speaker at the lectern (man about 50, glasses, kurta) looks at the meter, puzzled, while the whole room buzzes with motion. Lighting: warm hall lighting, slightly hazy. Mood: real motion that cancels out. Labels: "YES" over a nodding group, "NO" over a shaking group, "AVERAGE" on the meter.

key: Earthquakes come with aftershocks.
name: ch10_quake_aftershocks
alt: After a big earthquake, residents camp outside their houses for a shaky week, not knowing which way the ground will move next but sure it will keep moving.
scene: A small hill town the morning after a strong earthquake. Cracks run across a road and a few roof tiles have fallen; a temple bell lies on its side. A family has set up a temporary camp in an open field outside their house: a tarpaulin tent, mattresses, a gas cylinder and a kettle. The father (about 40, shawl over his shoulders) sits on a trunk looking at the ground, and the mother (about 38, cardigan over her sari) holds a cup of tea which ripples in small rings. A small boy points at a hanging lantern swinging slightly. Along the bottom of the image, a seismograph-style strip runs across the scene like a ribbon: one huge spike on the left for the main quake, followed by many smaller jagged spikes clustered close after it, slowly thinning out to the right. Above the family, a compass rose floats with arrows in every direction and a big question mark in the middle, showing the direction is unknown. A calendar beside the tent shows the coming week circled with small wobble marks on each day. Lighting: pale grey morning, dust still hanging in the air. Mood: uneasy, alert waiting. Labels: "QUAKE" over the big spike, "AFTERSHOCKS" over the cluster of smaller spikes.

key: A well-run railway: trains are on time
name: ch10_railway_signal_backlog
alt: A railway runs on time until a signal fails and trains back up, and the repair crew earns its pay fixing exactly that backlog.
scene: A wide aerial-style view of a big railway junction with many parallel tracks, a station with a clock tower, and a signal gantry. On most tracks, passenger trains glide along smoothly and evenly spaced; the station clock shows the trains exactly on time and small green lamps glow above them. On one track, the signal light on the gantry has failed, showing a broken bulb and a little puff of smoke, and behind it a long queue of trains has bunched up nose to tail, passengers leaning out of windows with frustrated faces and a man with a tiffin box checking his watch. Walking along the track toward the failed signal comes a repair crew of three engineers in orange overalls and hard hats, carrying a toolbox, a ladder and a new lamp, purposeful and calm. A small paper envelope with a rupee symbol floats above the crew leader, showing they are paid for exactly these moments. On the platform, a station master in a white uniform waves a green flag at the other trains that keep running. Lighting: bright midday sun, glinting rails. Mood: rare breakdowns are the paying work. Labels: "ON TIME" over the smooth tracks, "BACKLOG" over the bunched trains.

key: A restaurant review. A rave fills
name: ch10_review_makes_itself_true
alt: One restaurant gets a rave review, fills up and hires a better chef, while another gets a savage review, empties, and loses its good chef.
scene: A split-panel illustration of two restaurants across a street from each other, each with a newspaper review pinned in its window. LEFT panel: a newspaper clipping with five bright stars in the window; the restaurant is packed, every table full, a queue out the door, a happy owner counting money at the till. Through the kitchen hatch, a new star chef in a tall white hat (woman about 35) is being welcomed by the owner with a handshake, and the plates coming out look even better. A circular arrow drawn around the panel loops from the review to the crowd, to the money, to the chef, to better food and back to the review. RIGHT panel: a clipping with a single star and a big frown face in the window; the restaurant is empty, chairs stacked on tables, a waiter idly flicking a cloth. Through the back door, a good chef (man about 45, apron folded over his arm, suitcase in hand) is walking out to a waiting auto-rickshaw, and the food left on the counter looks dull. The same kind of circular arrow loops here, but downward. Lighting: warm, bustling light on the left; dim, cold light on the right. Mood: a forecast that makes itself come true. Labels: "RAVE" over the left window, "SAVAGE" over the right window.

key: Foxes and rabbits on an island.
name: ch10_foxes_rabbits_cycle
alt: On a small island, four scenes around a circle show rabbits multiplying, foxes multiplying, rabbits dwindling and foxes dwindling, round and round.
scene: A small grassy island surrounded by blue sea, seen from above at a gentle angle, with a lighthouse on one rocky edge. The island is divided into four quarter scenes arranged clockwise around a big circular arrow in the centre. Top: a meadow crowded with dozens of rabbits nibbling grass, and two lean foxes peeking from bushes with hungry eyes. Right: many plump foxes lounging and a few cubs playing, with fewer rabbits darting into burrows. Bottom: hardly any rabbits left, bare patches of ground, and thin foxes sitting around looking hungry and tired. Left: only a couple of foxes remain, wandering away, while baby rabbits are emerging from burrows and grass is growing back thick and green. The big circular arrow in the middle connects the four scenes and loops endlessly, with no trophy or winner's podium anywhere; a small empty podium at the centre of the arrow has a cobweb on it. Seagulls fly overhead and waves lap at the shore. Lighting: soft, natural daylight, changing slightly from lush to dry around the circle. Mood: an endless natural cycle, no winner. Labels: "RABBITS" on the top scene, "FOXES" on the right scene.

key: A doctor with years of bedside
name: ch11_doctor_eye_and_blood_test
alt: An experienced doctor examines a patient and points to where to look, while a lab report beside her confirms or rejects what she suspects.
scene: A clinic room in a small-town hospital with a steel examination bed, a green curtain and a window with a neem tree outside. An experienced doctor (woman about 55, grey streaks in her hair, white coat, stethoscope round her neck, reading glasses on a chain) sits on a stool beside an elderly patient (man about 70, kurta, thin, worried face) and gently presses below his eye to look at the colour of his eyelid, her expression sharp and attentive. A thought bubble above her shows a small magnifying glass hovering over the patient's eye and a guess with a question mark. On a tray next to her lies a printed blood test report in a clear plastic sleeve, with a short list of values and one value circled, and a test tube rack with a small labelled sample. A dotted arrow runs from her thought bubble to the report, and a second dotted arrow runs back from the report to her, closing the loop: her eye says where to look, the test says whether it is real. A young nurse (about 25, blue uniform) stands at the door holding a clipboard. Lighting: soft daylight through the window, clean clinical tones. Mood: experience and measurement working together. Labels: "EYE" beside the thought bubble, "TEST" on the report.

key: A 1.5-metre wave. At a calm lake
name: ch11_same_wave_lake_vs_beach
alt: The same size wave makes news at a calm lake where people gasp, but goes unnoticed at a surf beach where far bigger waves are normal.
scene: A split-panel illustration. LEFT panel: a calm hill-station lake with paddle boats shaped like swans, a wooden jetty and a promenade. A single wave of exactly the same height rises in the middle of the lake, tipping a paddle boat; people on the jetty gasp and point, a TV reporter with a microphone and a cameraman rush toward it, and a small newspaper boy holds up a paper with a big wave drawing on the front. A vertical measuring stick beside the wave shows its height. RIGHT panel: a wild surf beach on the western coast with big rolling breakers. The very same wave, with the same measuring stick at the same height, rolls in among much taller waves around it. Surfers paddle past without looking, a lifeguard in a tall chair reads a book, a family eats corn on the sand, nobody looks up. Beside each panel, a small ruler is drawn, and below it, a second short scale shows the size compared to normal waves of that place: high on the lake, low at the beach. Lighting: still pastel morning on the lake, bright breezy afternoon at the beach. Mood: big depends on where you are. Labels: "LAKE" at the top of the left panel, "SURF BEACH" at the top of the right panel.

key: Sorting coins into jars by size.
name: ch11_coins_into_jars
alt: A shopkeeper sorts a heap of mixed coins into a row of jars, and the jar heights show which sizes are common and which are rare, with insets showing too few or too many jars.
scene: A kirana shop counter at closing time, with sacks of rice and shelves of packets behind. A shopkeeper (man about 50, half-sleeve shirt, spectacles pushed up, a cloth bag beside him) pours a heap of mixed coins from the day's takings onto the counter and drops them one by one into a neat row of eight glass jars, each jar labelled by coin size, smallest on the left. The jars fill to different heights: a few coins in the far left and far right jars, many in the middle jars, forming a hump shape that is easy to see at a glance. A dotted curve is drawn across the tops of the coin piles. The order in which the coins arrived is lost, shown by a faded notepad with a crossed-out time list. Two small insets sit below the counter. In the first, only two huge jars hold all the coins, and the hump shape is hidden. In the second, forty tiny jars stand in a long row, each holding just one coin, a flat confusing row. His young daughter (about 10, school uniform) watches the main row, pointing at the tallest jar. Lighting: warm yellow bulb light, evening outside. Mood: counting reveals the shape. Labels: "COMMON" over the tall middle jars, "RARE" over the end jars.

key: A fat-tailed curve is a bell with
name: ch11_bell_with_trapdoors
alt: Two hills of the same bell shape look alike in the middle, but one hides trapdoors far out on its edges where hikers fall through.
scene: A wide, gentle landscape showing two smooth grassy hills side by side, each shaped like a bell, with a gentle hump in the middle and long flat slopes stretching far to each side. On both hills, families stroll along the gentle middle section, a couple with a picnic basket, a child flying a kite, an old man with a walking stick; the two middles look identical. Far out on the flat outer slopes of the right-hand hill, several square trapdoors are cut into the grass, almost invisible, drawn with faint outlines and small hinges. One trapdoor has swung open beneath a hiker (young man, backpack, cap) who is dropping through with a shocked face, his hat flying off; another hiker further out peers nervously at a square outline at his feet. A cutaway at the edge of the right hill reveals deep pits under the trapdoors. The left hill's outer slopes are solid ground with grazing goats. A small signboard at the foot of the right hill shows a bell symbol with a hidden exclamation mark. Lighting: pleasant afternoon light, long shadows. Mood: looks safe, until the edges. Labels: "NORMAL" over the left hill, "FAT TAILS" over the right hill, "TRAPDOOR" by the open door.

key: The mean wealth of the customers is now
name: ch11_billionaire_in_cafe
alt: An anonymous billionaire in a suit walks into a café full of students, and two signs show the average wealth shooting up while the typical customer is still a student with a coffee.
scene: A cosy college-area café with wooden tables, chalkboard menu and fairy lights. About a dozen customers sit around: students with laptops and backpacks, a girl with headphones sipping cold coffee, two boys sharing a sandwich, a young man counting coins for his bill. Through the door strides an anonymous very rich man, seen from behind and the side with his face turned away (tall, sharp dark suit, shiny shoes), trailing a long shimmering gold glow and a few floating banknote icons behind him. On the wall above the counter hang two old-fashioned display boards. The first board's number has just spun up wildly to a huge figure with many zeros, the digits blurring, a small rocket icon beside it. The second board shows a picture of an ordinary student with a coffee cup, unchanged, with a small calm tick beside it. A barista (woman about 25, apron, cap) looks from one board to the other with raised eyebrows. In a small line of customers drawn in order from poorest to richest along the bottom, a finger points to the one in the exact middle, still a student. Lighting: warm café glow with a golden flash around the newcomer. Mood: one outlier moves the average, not the middle. Labels: "MEAN" on the first board, "MEDIAN" on the second board.

key: SD is a smoke detector that screams
name: ch11_detector_vs_thermostat
alt: In a living room a ceiling smoke detector shrieks at a single burnt match, while a wall thermostat in the middle of the room does not register it at all.
scene: A living room in an apartment, seen from a corner, with a sofa, a coffee table and a small prayer shelf with a lamp. In the middle of the coffee table, a young woman (about 28, kurta, hair clipped up) holds a single burnt-out matchstick with a thin wisp of smoke after lighting the lamp. On the ceiling directly above, a round smoke detector shrieks with huge zigzag sound waves and a flashing red light, wildly out of proportion to the tiny wisp, and a cat leaps off the sofa in fright. On the side wall, a beige thermostat with a digital display shows a calm, unchanged reading and a small sleeping face icon, completely unaware of the match. Two small dotted arrows go from the wisp of smoke: one shoots up to the detector with an exclamation mark, the other fades out before reaching the thermostat. A small inset at the top corner shows the reverse case: the whole room slowly warming on a hot afternoon, the thermostat noticing it with a rising arrow while the smoke detector stays silent. Lighting: warm evening lamplight, red flashes from the detector. Mood: each instrument misses what the other catches. Labels: "SD" next to the smoke detector, "IQR" next to the thermostat.

key: spirit level and square do most of
name: ch11_tape_vs_laser_scanner
alt: A carpenter's simple tape, level and square do the job reliably, while a fancy laser scanner confidently measures a reflection in a mirror.
scene: A half-finished room in a house under renovation, with bare plaster walls, sawhorses and a large mirror leaning against one wall. On the left, an older carpenter (about 55, faded checked shirt, pencil behind his ear, measuring tape clipped to his belt) kneels and checks a wooden shelf with a spirit level, the bubble neatly centred, a steel square and a tape lying beside him, a neat finished shelf on the wall above him. On the right, a young technician (about 25, slick jacket, lanyard, smart glasses) holds up a sleek handheld laser scanner that projects a glowing red grid. He aims it at the mirror, and the laser beam bounces off the glass and measures a whole ghost room that is only a reflection; a floating readout above his scanner shows a big confident number with a green tick, while the ghost room in the mirror is drawn as faint dotted lines that do not exist. The technician smiles proudly, unaware. A small dotted arrow traces the beam from the scanner into the mirror and back. Lighting: dusty afternoon light through an unfinished window. Mood: simple reliable tools versus confident nonsense. Labels: "TAPE" beside the tape measure, "REFLECTION" on the mirror.

key: A courtroom. The defendant (your edge)
name: ch11_courtroom_edge_on_trial
alt: In a courtroom a nervous defendant labelled as the trading edge stands trial, and the judge weighs the evidence on scales against coincidence.
scene: A traditional Indian courtroom with high ceilings, ceiling fans, wooden benches and a raised judge's bench. A judge (woman about 55, black robe, white collar bands, spectacles) sits high at the bench with a gavel. In the dock stands the defendant, a small nervous figure (young man in a plain shirt) with a paper sign hung on his chest showing a small upward-arrow chart, representing the trading edge; he wrings his hands. In front of the judge, a large brass balance scale holds a pile of evidence files on one pan, and on the other pan a set of dice and a spinning coin representing coincidence. A lawyer in a black coat lays another file on the evidence pan. A small dotted bar above the scale shows a threshold line that the evidence must cross. In the public gallery, a few traders lean forward anxiously. A clerk at a typewriter is typing the verdict, which reads only not proven, not innocent, on a slip half out of the machine. Lighting: hazy daylight from tall windows, dust in the beams. Mood: proof beyond reasonable doubt. Labels: "EVIDENCE" on the files pan, "CHANCE" on the dice pan.

key: A straight road seen through a rainy
name: ch11_road_through_rainy_windscreen
alt: From a driver's seat, the same straight road is clearly visible through a lightly wet windscreen but almost invisible through heavy rain.
scene: A split-panel illustration from inside a car, looking out through the windscreen at a straight highway running through flat countryside with a line of trees. Both panels show exactly the same road, with the same white centre line running straight to the horizon and the same distant water tower. LEFT panel: a light drizzle, only a few scattered drops on the glass; the driver's hands (man's, wristwatch, steering wheel with a small idol on the dashboard) rest relaxed on the wheel and the road and its centre line are clearly visible. RIGHT panel: a heavy monsoon downpour streams over the windscreen in thick sheets, the wipers mid-swipe, and the road and its centre line are barely visible, just a faint smeared shape; the driver's hands grip the wheel tightly, leaning forward, and a small question mark floats in the fogged corner of the glass. A thin faint dashed line is drawn over the true road in both panels to show that the road itself is identical. Lighting: soft grey daylight on the left, dark stormy light with headlight glare on the right. Mood: the line is the same, the noise decides if you can see it. Labels: "LIGHT RAIN" at the top of the left panel, "HEAVY RAIN" at the top of the right panel.

key: Polling 200 people about the weather
name: ch11_poll_one_street
alt: A pollster interviews a huge crowd about the weather, but all of them are standing on the same rainy street, so 200 answers amount to one observation.
scene: A narrow city street in heavy rain, crowded shoulder to shoulder with about two hundred people under umbrellas and raincoats, packed between old buildings with balconies and shop signs. At the front, an eager young pollster (woman about 26, clear raincoat, clipboard sealed in a plastic bag, lanyard) moves through the crowd with a microphone, and every person she points the microphone at says the same thing, shown as many identical speech bubbles with a little rain-cloud icon. Her clipboard shows a long column of tally marks, all in the same box. Above the street, a single dark rain cloud sits exactly over the crowd, and beyond the rooftops, small views of other neighbourhoods are visible: one sunny with kids playing cricket, another misty, another with a rainbow, none of which have been asked. A dotted outline circles the whole crowd and labels it as just one point. An older colleague (man about 50, umbrella, glasses) taps her on the shoulder and gestures toward the other neighbourhoods. Lighting: grey rainy light, wet reflections on the street. Mood: many answers, one observation. Labels: "200 ANSWERS" over the crowd, "1 STREET" on the dotted outline.

key: Two archers whose average arrow is
name: ch11_two_archers_spread
alt: Two archery targets show arrows grouped tightly at two clearly different points, while two other targets show arrows scattered so widely that a small gap in their averages means nothing.
scene: An archery range on a sunny field with a row of four straw targets on wooden stands, a white line in the grass and two archers standing at the line (a young woman in a tracksuit and a middle-aged man in a vest, both with bows lowered, looking at the targets). The targets are arranged in two pairs. The LEFT pair: on each target, the arrows are bunched in a tight cluster the size of a coin, one cluster slightly left of centre and the other slightly right; a small ruler drawn between the two cluster centres shows a short gap, and it is obvious the two archers aimed at different points. The RIGHT pair: on each target, the arrows are scattered widely across every ring, some on the edge, some near the bullseye; a small dot marks the average point of each spread, and the same short ruler sits between the two dots, but the clouds of arrows overlap so much that the gap looks meaningless. A coach (woman about 50, cap, whistle) points at the tight pair with a nod and shrugs at the scattered pair. Lighting: bright midday sun, crisp shadows of the arrows. Mood: a gap only means something if the spread is small. Labels: "TIGHT" over the left pair, "SCATTERED" over the right pair.

key: A car test drive that includes a
name: ch12_test_drive_route_map
alt: A test driver's route map covers a motorway, a traffic jam and a mountain pass, with an off-road track on the map clearly marked as not tested.
scene: A wide illustrated map, like a tourist map seen from above at an angle, with a small white test car driving a looping route. The route passes through three clearly drawn zones, each with a green tick flag: on the left, a wide straight motorway with the car cruising fast past green fields; in the middle, a busy city section with the car stuck in a traffic jam among buses, autos and a cow; on the right, a winding mountain pass with hairpin bends and pine trees, the car climbing carefully. In the lower corner of the map, a rough muddy off-road track with rocks, puddles and a stream crossing is drawn but fenced off with a red-and-white barrier, a red cross flag and the car's route clearly not entering it. In the foreground at the edge of the map sits the test driver (woman about 35, racing jacket, sunglasses pushed up) holding a clipboard checklist with three ticks and one box clearly marked with a cross, nodding with satisfaction and honesty. Beside her, an engineer (man about 45, overalls) points at the fenced-off track. Lighting: bright, clear day across the whole map. Mood: thorough, and honest about the gaps. Labels: "TESTED" near the three ticked zones, "NOT TESTED" by the off-road track.

key: split the population into groups you
name: ch12_stratified_jury_draw
alt: A court clerk picks jurors by drawing at random from separate boxes for each group of people, instead of taking the first names off a phone list.
scene: A split-panel illustration in a court records office. LEFT panel, the wrong way: a bored clerk (man about 40, half-sleeve shirt, pen behind his ear) runs his finger down the first page of a thick phone directory, picking the top names; all the chosen name cards on his desk start with the same letter, and the little juror figures standing behind him all look alike, same age, same clothes. A red cross sits above this panel. RIGHT panel, the right way: a careful clerk (woman about 45, cotton sari, spectacles, lanyard) stands at a long table with a row of six glass lottery drums, each drum filled with folded slips and labelled by a simple icon for a group: young, old, city, village, men, women. She turns each drum's handle and pulls one slip at random from inside it with a calm, fair expression. Behind her, the jurors selected stand in a varied row: a farmer with a turban, a college student, an elderly woman, a businessman, a nurse, a young mechanic. A green tick sits above this panel. Lighting: tube lights, files stacked high, steady daylight from a window. Mood: fairness by design. Labels: "FIRST 200" at the top of the left panel, "RANDOM IN EACH GROUP" at the top of the right panel.

key: An index is a class photo taken
name: ch12_slow_shutter_class_photo
alt: A school class photo taken with a slow shutter shows some children sharp and some blurred because they moved, next to a set of crisp individual portraits.
scene: A school courtyard with a banner strung between two pillars, a wooden bench arrangement and a big old camera on a tripod under a black cloth. The main image is the resulting class photo, shown large in a wooden frame: about fifty children in uniform arranged in three rows, a teacher seated in the middle. Most faces are sharp, but several children appear smeared and ghostly because they moved during the long exposure: a boy who turned to whisper to his neighbour shows two overlapping heads, a girl who waved has a fan of blurred arms, a boy at the end who sneezed is a streak. Small motion arrows show which way each moved. The blurs form their own pattern, more toward the edges of the rows. Beside the framed photo, pinned on a board, are a neat grid of small crisp individual passport-style portraits of the same children, each sharp and still. The photographer (old man, white kurta, cap, cloth draped over his shoulder) stands beside the camera holding a pocket watch, the shutter left open. Lighting: hazy sunlight in the courtyard. Mood: a real picture, but not the same as sharp portraits. Labels: "INDEX" on the class photo frame, "STOCKS" over the portrait grid.

key: Clouds. Everyone sees a dragon
name: ch12_clouds_look_like_charts
alt: People lying on a hillside see a dragon and a face in the clouds, and one cloud looks exactly like a textbook double top chart pattern.
scene: A grassy hillside on a breezy summer afternoon with a wide blue sky full of fluffy white clouds. Lying on their backs on a picnic mat are three friends: a young woman (about 25, kurta, sunglasses on her head) pointing up and laughing, a young man (about 27, T-shirt, cap over his eyes) pointing at a different cloud, and an older man (about 55, spectacles, a trading magazine resting on his chest) staring up with a serious, analytical face. Above them, one cloud clearly looks like a dragon with wings, another looks like a smiling face with puffy cheeks, and a third long cloud has a very clear outline of two equal humps side by side with a dip between them, exactly like a double-top chart pattern; a faint thin line is drawn under its humps as the older man traces it with his finger. A fourth cloud has a sharp upward step like a breakout. Nobody has packed a suitcase or started a journey toward the dragon; the picnic basket sits unmoved beside them. A kite drifts in the wind across the clouds. Lighting: bright, soft afternoon light. Mood: patterns are everywhere in randomness. Labels: "DRAGON" near the dragon cloud, "DOUBLE TOP" near the two-hump cloud.

key: Judging a striker by the team
name: ch12_striker_shots_not_score
alt: A scout ignores the final scoreboard and watches each of a striker's shots one by one, ticking them in a notebook, while rain and a goalkeeper also shape the score.
scene: A local football ground on a rainy evening with floodlights and muddy patches. A young striker (about 20, jersey number nine, shin pads, determined face) strikes the ball toward the goal while a tall goalkeeper (about 25, gloves, bright kit) dives. Heavy rain slants across the pitch, and the scoreboard above the stand shows a final losing score. In the foreground stand two observers. On the left, a loud fan (man about 45, raincoat, scarf) points angrily at the scoreboard and waves his hand at the striker, judging by the result. On the right, a calm scout (woman about 40, hooded rain jacket, notebook in a plastic sleeve) ignores the scoreboard entirely and watches the striker; her notebook has a row of small sketches of each shot, numbered one to eight, each with a tick or a cross by how well it was struck. Thin dotted arrows from the striker's boot to each sketch in her notebook show she tracks every shot individually. Small labels of other factors float around the scoreboard: a goalkeeper glove icon and a raincloud icon, both feeding into the score. Lighting: white floodlights, sheets of rain, reflective puddles. Mood: judge the shots, not the scoreline. Labels: "SCORE" on the scoreboard, "SHOTS" over the scout's notebook.

key: A ruler that resets its length
name: ch13_stretchy_ruler_legs
alt: A tailor's elastic ruler marked 0 to 1 is stretched to fit a small swing and a huge swing, so the pullbacks on both are read as the same fractions.
scene: A tailor's workshop with bolts of cloth, a sewing machine and a mirror. On a long cutting table, two pieces of cloth are laid out, one short and narrow, one very long and wide, each with a zigzag line chalked on it showing a climb, a dip back and another climb, like a mountain path. A tailor (man about 50, round glasses, measuring tape around his neck, kurta with rolled sleeves) uses a special elastic ruler, a band of rubber printed with evenly spaced marks from 0 at one end to 1 at the other, with small marks in between. On the short cloth, he stretches it just a little so 0 sits at the bottom of the first climb and 1 at its top. On the long cloth, his apprentice (young woman about 20, plait, thimble on her finger) stretches an identical band much further so its 0 and 1 again fit the first climb exactly. Thin dotted lines drop from the bottom of each dip onto the elastic bands, landing on the same mark on both, despite the very different sizes. A price tag with a small amount sits on the short cloth and a tag with a large amount on the long one. Lighting: warm workshop light, dust in the air. Mood: everything measured in the same units. Labels: "0" at the band's start, "1" at the band's end, "SAME FRACTION" between the two dips.

key: A class average where one student
name: ch14_class_average_one_mark
alt: A teacher of a huge class barely notices one changing mark, while a teacher with only three students sees the class average swing wildly.
scene: A split-panel illustration of two classrooms at the end of a school day, both with a ringing bell on the wall. LEFT panel: a huge lecture hall with two hundred students in tiered rows. A board at the front shows the class average as a large steady number on a dial. One student in the middle (boy, about 16, glasses) has a mark card that keeps flipping between numbers, drawn with motion lines, but the dial on the board barely trembles; the teacher (man about 50, half-sleeve shirt) sips tea calmly without looking. RIGHT panel: a tiny tutoring room with just three students at one table. The same kind of boy's mark card flips between numbers, and the class average dial on the small whiteboard swings wildly back and forth with large motion arcs. The tutor (woman about 35, cotton sari, glasses) stares at the swinging dial, alarmed, chalk frozen in her hand, while the other two students look on. A small dotted arrow in each panel connects the flipping card to the dial, thick and strong in the small room, thin and weak in the big hall. A wall clock in both panels shows a few seconds before the bell. Lighting: late afternoon sun through windows. Mood: few members, big swings. Labels: "200" above the hall, "3" above the small room.

key: A finish line that walks toward
name: ch14_walking_finish_line
alt: A runner has stopped short of a finish line, and over the day the painted line slides along the track on wheels until it touches her footprint, making a photo look like she reached it.
scene: A wide view of a running track in a small stadium, drawn as a time-lapse across one day. In the foreground, a runner (woman about 25, vest, shorts, bib number) stands a few metres short of a white finish line, having stopped early in the morning; she sits on the grass beside her own last footprint, eating a banana, relaxed. Her footprint on the track is circled. The finish line is painted on a long wooden board mounted on small wheels, and a series of ghost copies of the board shows it slowly rolling along the track toward the footprint across the day, with a sun moving from morning to evening along the top of the image. In the final position, at sunset, the board's line sits exactly on the footprint. On the right, a photographer (man about 40, cap, camera with a big lens) snaps a picture at sunset; a small inset of his photo shows the runner's foot touching the finish line, looking like a perfect finish. A small dotted arrow on the track traces the line's movement. Lighting: morning light on the left fading to orange sunset on the right. Mood: the line came to the runner, not the other way round. Labels: "FINISH LINE" on the board, "FOOTPRINT" by the circled print.

key: Before testing a car you test the
name: ch14_test_bricks_before_car
alt: Engineers test individual bricks before building a car from them, and one brick crumbles into sand under the press.
scene: A quirky workshop where a car is being built from bricks like a toy, half finished on a stand in the background, with a sleek designer drawing pinned to the wall. In the foreground, two engineers (woman about 40, safety goggles, lab coat; and young man about 25, overalls, gloves) stand at a heavy hydraulic press testing the bricks one at a time before they go into the car. A conveyor belt brings bricks from the left. Most bricks on a tray to the right of the press are solid and stamped with green ticks. The brick currently under the press has crumbled into a heap of loose sand, grains spilling over the edge, and both engineers stare at it with raised eyebrows. A dotted arrow runs from the sand heap to the half-built car, where one brick in the car's frame is highlighted in red, showing that it would bring the whole car down. A clipboard hanging on the press lists bricks with a column of ticks and one cross. In the background, a designer (man about 50, bow tie) proudly holds up the clever car drawing, unaware. Lighting: bright workshop lights, a cloud of dust from the crumbled brick. Mood: check the foundations first. Labels: "BRICK TEST" on the press, "SAND" by the crumbled brick.

key: A fence everyone says matters.
name: ch14_fence_cows_wander
alt: Villagers expect a stampede when cows push through a famous fence, but in one field the cows wander back a little and in another they simply keep grazing.
scene: A wide rural scene with a long wooden fence running across green fields, villagers gathered along it. A large signboard by the fence shows a dramatic painting of cows stampeding, expressing what everyone expects. On the left, a group of villagers (a man with a turban and a stick, a woman with a water pot, two boys) lean on the fence with wide eyes, bracing for a stampede. In the middle field, a few cows have pushed through a gap in the fence; instead of charging off, they amble a few steps and then wander back slightly toward the fence, one of them chewing grass lazily, shown with a small curved arrow back. In the right field, divided by a low wall, a different herd has crossed the same fence and does not react at all, simply grazing with heads down, a cow lying in the shade, a bird on one cow's back. A farmer in the right field (old man, white dhoti, cap) shrugs at the watching villagers. Small plaque-like tags are planted in each field. Lighting: soft late-morning sun, long grass shimmering. Mood: much talked about, little effect. Labels: "STOCKS" in the middle field, "FUTURES" in the right field, "STAMPEDE?" on the signboard.

key: Swimming only when the sea is calm.
name: ch14_swim_only_calm_sea
alt: A swimmer checks a beach flag and swims only on calm days, missing a few good swims but staying out of nearly every storm, which come mostly at low tide.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same beach with a lifeguard tower and a flag pole. LEFT panel: a calm morning with a green flag, gentle waves and a high tide line close to the dunes; a middle-aged swimmer (woman about 45, swimming cap, goggles on her forehead, towel over her shoulder) wades in happily, while a few cheerful swimmers already float in the water. RIGHT panel: a stormy afternoon with a red flag, huge crashing waves, dark clouds and lightning; the tide has gone far out, exposing wet sand and rocks, and an arrow on the sand shows the water retreating. The same woman sits dry on the dunes under a beach umbrella with a flask of tea, watching, safe. In the water, a lone swimmer struggles among the big waves while a lifeguard runs toward him. A small inset at the top of the right panel shows a third scene: a nice sunny day with a yellow flag where she also stayed out, missing a good swim, with a small shrug. A small calendar beside the flag pole shows most storm days clustered under a low-tide icon. Lighting: bright calm light on the left, dark and dramatic on the right. Mood: skip the risky days, accept missing some good ones. Labels: "CALM" at the top of the left panel, "STORM" at the top of the right panel.

key: The moving average is a useful ruler
name: ch14_ruler_not_wall_but_storm_flag
alt: On a harbour master's desk a ruler is ticked as useful, a wall, a crystal ball and a compass are crossed out, and a storm warning flag is ticked.
scene: The wooden desk of a harbour master's office by the sea, viewed from slightly above, with a window behind showing boats and a grey sky. Five objects are laid out in a row across the desk, each with a small tag. First, a long brass ruler lying across a chart of past ship positions, measuring where they have been, with a green tick. Second, a small model of a brick wall, with a red cross over it. Third, a glowing crystal ball on a stand, with a red cross over it. Fourth, an old compass with its needle spinning, with a red cross over it. Fifth, a small triangular red storm warning flag on a mini flagpole, with a green tick and a small lightning bolt beside it. The harbour master (woman about 50, navy jacket with brass buttons, cap, reading glasses) stands behind the desk holding the ruler in one hand and reaching for the storm flag with the other, while outside the window a few fishing boats head back toward the harbour under darkening clouds. Lighting: warm desk lamp against cool grey light from the window. Mood: know what your tool is good for. Labels: "RULER" by the ruler, "STORM WARNING" by the flag.
